BLD-anchor_matching.content:
For each native-GPS photo of a (camera group, destination, day) bucket, `frame_candidates` SHALL take every track
point within `gpx_anchor_max_point_distance_meters` of it and every segment — two consecutive points at most
`gpx_interpolation_max_gap_seconds` apart — within `gpx_anchor_max_segment_distance_meters`, each at a time within
`gpx_anchor_max_clock_error_seconds` of the photo's camera time read as UTC; split them into passes where more than
`gpx_interpolation_max_gap_seconds` separates two in time; and keep each pass's best, a point before a segment, then the
closest. `infer_anchor_proposal` clusters the candidates' offsets within `gpx_anchor_offset_spread_max_seconds` and
proposes the cluster the most photos support, a tie going to the smaller offset, its best-ranked candidate the
representative; its confidence is `review_required` when a photo supports no pass of it or another cluster ties
(`tied`), else `high` when another photo supports it or it is a point match, else `medium`. Only an agreed offset — no
conflicting photo, no tie — applies itself, under `multi_anchor_auto_apply` or `single_anchor_auto_apply`. The proposal
names the photos no pass of which agrees (`conflicting_files`), and each cluster in `groups` with its photo count and a
representative, its track file included; a `manual_offset_seconds` within `gpx_anchor_offset_spread_max_seconds` of a
group's offset takes effect as `gpx_anchor_chosen`, which no drift check follows.

`geotag finalize` SHALL write `photos-26-complete-log.json` and the database snapshot `photos-26-geotag-ingest.db`, then

plan and track memos `photos-00-plan-memo.db` and `photos-00-track-memo.db`, and any `*-archive.tar.gz` — with its SHA-256 and path in
`photos-26-archive-manifest.json`, recording the workspace's identity — the init run id prep wrote in the guard — with
the folder's name beside it, and the plan and execution ids, and archive those files and the manifest into
`photos-26-archive.tar.gz` in the control directory, by a temporary name and an atomic rename — writing nothing else,
and requiring a ready plan whose execution succeeded (geotag §31). Merge's re-seal does the same into
`photos-35-archive-manifest.json` and `photos-35-archive.tar.gz` (§13.6).

BLD-artifact_numbering.content:
The numbered artifacts SHALL follow this scheme:

```text
0X  workspace infrastructure (phase-neutral): config, guard, live database
1X  prep-phase artifacts        (currently: 10 = prep plan, 11 = handoff, 15 = prep audit log + prep DB snapshot)
2X  geotag-phase artifacts        (currently: 21–26; 26 = complete log + geotag DB snapshot + archive manifest)
3X  merge-phase artifacts        (currently: 30 = merge plan, 31 = merge summary, 35 = merge log + merge DB snapshot + archive manifest)
```

The first digit means only the producing phase. The second is a sequence number within the phase with no
further meaning: an absent number is not reserved, not headroom and not missing, and nothing is to be inferred from a
gap. Sibling end-of-phase records that differ only by extension MAY share a number — `photos-15-prep-log.json` and
`photos-15-prep-ingest.db` are both the end-of-prep record, one the human-readable log and one the database image;
likewise `photos-26-complete-log.json`, `photos-26-geotag-ingest.db` and `photos-26-archive-manifest.json`, and the
three `photos-35` files. The full filename — number, name and
extension — is the identifier, never the number alone; `photos-0X-*` (and `1X`, `2X`, `3X`) names a band. The
bands are unrelated to the numbered media folders `0-sources`…`6-photos-by-dest`.

there is planned whatever it holds; each recognized move's `db_upsert` names the path it came from (`moved_from`), by
which prep's log finds the entry of a photo whose fingerprint changed with the move. The old path is left to the ghost
prunes; an unmatched row is a ghost, and its file is read as new.

BLD-control_directory_contents.content:
The control records SHALL be these files in `.photos-ingest/` ({need}`DEF-archival_package` and {need}`DEF-workspace_database` for the archival and database ones):

```text
.photos-ingest/
  photos-00-config.json            workspace configuration (seeded by prep, Section 4)
  photos-00-workspace.lock         the workspace lock: held by every run while it plans or executes (Section 2)
  photos-00-decision-editor.lock   the decision editor's lock: one editor at a time on a workspace
  photos-00-workspace-guard        workspace root sentinel: marks the workspace as INITIALIZED (written last by prep on init, prep photos-1-prep-workflow.md Section 3.1)
  photos-00-sealed.json            terminal/sealed marker, written by a successful merge ALONGSIDE the guard (a separate file, not a field inside the guard) — its presence seals the workspace (Section 13.7)
  photos-00-ingest.db              SQLite identity/metadata cache + derived caches (live working DB, Section 13.4)
  photos-00-plan-memo.db           prep-phase scratch: plan memo, what planning read of each media file (disposable, NOT part of the record)
  photos-00-track-memo.db          geotag-phase scratch: each track file's parsed points, by the SHA-256 of its bytes (disposable, NOT part of the record)
  photos-15-prep-ingest.db         prep-phase artifact: DB backup snapshot, end of prep (Section 13.4a)
  journal-*.json                   execution journals
  photos-10-prep-plan.json         prep-phase artifact: prep plan (written by `plan`, consumed by `dry-run`/`execute`; see "Canonical plan persistence" below)
  photos-11-handoff.json           prep-phase artifact: handoff manifest
  photos-15-prep-log.json          prep-phase artifact: end-of-prep audit log (Section 13.3 / prep 16.1)
  photos-21-time-decisions.json    geotag-phase artifact
  photos-22-gps-drift-validation.json  geotag-phase artifact: GPS-drift validation gate (§22a)
  photos-23-gps-decisions.json     geotag-phase artifact
  photos-24-executable-plan.json   geotag-phase artifact
  photos-25-execution-summary.json geotag-phase artifact
  photos-26-complete-log.json      geotag-phase artifact: full transformation log (prep+geotag, at finalize, Section 13.3)
  photos-26-geotag-ingest.db       geotag-phase artifact: DB backup snapshot, end of geotag (Section 13.4a)
  photos-26-finalized-media.json   geotag-phase artifact: each by-dest photo's size and mtime as finalize found it
  photos-26-archive-manifest.json  geotag-phase artifact: the archival package's manifest, at finalize (Section 13.2)
  photos-26-archive.tar.gz         geotag-phase artifact: the archival package, at finalize (Section 13.2)
  photos-30-merge-plan.json        merge-phase artifact: merge plan (written by `plan`, consumed by `dry-run`/`execute`)
  photos-31-merge-summary.json     merge-phase artifact: library-merge summary (Section 13.5)
  photos-35-merge-log.json         merge-phase artifact: full transformation log (prep+geotag+merge, Section 13.3)
  photos-35-merge-ingest.db        merge-phase artifact: DB backup snapshot, end of merge (Section 13.4a)
  photos-35-archive-manifest.json  merge-phase artifact: the re-sealed package's manifest, superseding photos-26's (Section 13.6)
  photos-35-archive.tar.gz         merge-phase artifact: the re-sealed archival package (Section 13.6)
  executed/<plan id>/              geotag: the decision records each executed plan ran against (Section 13.3a)
  <artifact>-NNN.<ext>             a superseded plan or decision record, kept when it was replaced (Section 5)
  gpx/                             gpx_root, when configured to live here (Section 8)
```

The section numbers in it are the shared contract's.

holds the handoff's content fingerprint, `camera_time_policy_fingerprint` — over the whole

BLD-drift_validation.aliases: geotag-drift-trigger-1, geotag-drift-gate-position-1, geotag-drift-confirmation-preserved-1, geotag-drift-corrected-validated-1, geotag-drift-not-mutate-21-1, geotag-drift-recompute-utc-1, geotag-drift-withdrawal-rejects-plan-1
BLD-drift_validation.content:
Once photos-21 is complete, `geotag plan` SHALL write `photos-22-gps-drift-validation.json` with a cell for each
offset cell whose effective source is `timezone_accepted` or `manual`, none of whose photos not yet corrected anchors on
the tracks, and whose photos' resolved times lie within `gpx_anchor_max_clock_error_seconds` of track points: its
`proposal` holding `current_offset_seconds`, its source, the photos and that track segment; its `user_decision`
`confirmed`, `corrected_offset_seconds` and `confirmed_offset_seconds`. A cell confirmed with `confirmed_offset_seconds`
equal to its current offset takes effect as `gps_drift_validated` — the current offset when no correction is given,
else the correction; confirmed against another offset it is `stale_user_decision` and takes no effect; confirmed
naming none, a blocker. Until every cell has taken effect, photos-23 and photos-24 are not written; then resolved UTC
is computed again with the validated offsets, photos-21 left as it is. photos-22's `depends_on` holds photos-21's
SHA-256, `gpx_fingerprint`, `camera_time_policy_fingerprint` and `camera_group_key_version`.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it

BLD-editor_checks_seal.content: `edit` SHALL refuse to serve a sealed workspace, with the same warning, its save writing nothing there.
BLD-editor_checks_seal.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-editor_checks_seal.title: The editor checks the seal

BLD-editor_save_locks.content:
The decision editor's save SHALL take the workspace lock for the time it writes, refusing at once while a run holds it;
the editor's display reads take none, each record being replaced whole.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-editor_save_locks.title: The editor's save takes the lock

BLD-executable_plan.content:
`photos-24-executable-plan.json` SHALL hold `status` — `ready`, or `blocked` with the plan's `blockers` — `executable`,
`depends_on`, `plan_id` (the first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 of `depends_on`), and per destination its `operations`,
`no_ops` (the photos it holds already as planned) and a `summary`. An operation is `metadata_time_write`, carrying the
resolved time, its rule, offset and timezone, and the decision it followed; `metadata_gps_write`, its origin
`apply_manual` — with the decision and the position it replaces — or `recompute_automated`; `gps_marker_write`, one that
clears geotag's position carrying the position it removes; or `rename_no_clobber`. A write the photo already holds is
not planned.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-executable_plan.title: The executable plan

BLD-execution_summary.content:
`photos-25-execution-summary.json` SHALL record the plan and execution ids, the SHA-256 of photos-24 and the
dependencies it was validated against, counts per destination and in total, what was newly applied and what found
satisfied, failures and blockers, `fingerprint_mismatches` — each with its expected and actual fingerprint and
`user_decision.accept_fingerprint_change`, the one field a later execution reads — the snapshot, and run metadata apart;
its `status` is `success`, `partial` (anything outstanding, a mismatch always), `failed` (nothing applied) or
`rejected` (stopped before any change). It is never a dependency.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-execution_summary.title: The execution summary

BLD-failed_fingerprint.content:
A fingerprint that could not be taken SHALL be recorded with the status `failed` and no value; prep's duplicate grouping
passes it over, its plan records a blocker for each such file outside `6-photos-by-dest`, and neither the workspace
database nor the plan memo offers it for reuse.
BLD-failed_fingerprint.section_name: 11. Duplicates and failures beside photos by destination
sections: 11. Duplicates and failures beside photos by destination
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-failed_fingerprint.title: A failed fingerprint is recorded as failed

BLD-failed_operation.content: Prep SHALL journal an operation that raised as `failed`, and stop.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-failed_operation.title: Prep's failed operation

BLD-filename_timestamp_format.content:
The format SHALL be the configuration key `filename_timestamp_format`, default `"%Y-%m-%d--%H-%M-%S"`, which gives a
timestamp of the form `YYYY-MM-DD--HH-MM-SS`. Both phases read it; geotag's plans also depend on it through the
filename-format fingerprint ({need}`DEF-dependency_cascade`).
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-filename_timestamp_format.title: `filename_timestamp_format`

BLD-finalize_checks_prep_log.content:
Geotag's finalize SHALL copy prep's log only when its bytes hash to the value {need}`BLD-prep_log_vouched` records, and
stop otherwise — the log missing or unreadable, or the handoff recording no hash, among the cases.
BLD-finalize_checks_prep_log.section_name: 5. What each of prep’s records depends on
sections: 5. What each of prep’s records depends on
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-finalize_checks_prep_log.title: Finalize copies only the log the handoff vouches for

BLD-finalize_preconditions.content:
`geotag finalize` SHALL refuse, writing nothing, unless `photos-24-executable-plan.json` is `ready`,
`photos-25-execution-summary.json` is `success` for the same `plan_id`, and every dependency of the plan but the
handoff still holds — the handoff left out because prep, run after execute, records geotag's own writes and renames
in it.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-finalize_preconditions.title: What finalize checks first

BLD-finalized_media.content:
`geotag finalize` SHALL write `photos-26-finalized-media.json`, giving each photo in photos by destination, under its
final path, its size and modification time; merge's preflight refuses when a photo still there differs from it, or the
record is missing.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-finalized_media.title: Each photo as finalize found it

BLD-fingerprint.content:
A photo's fingerprint SHALL be ImageMagick `identify`'s signature — a SHA-256 of the normalized pixel stream; a video's,
the `ffmpeg` MD5 of its streams as stored, copied out without decoding (`-c copy`).
BLD-fingerprint.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-fingerprint.title: How a fingerprint is computed

BLD-fingerprint_method.content:
Each fingerprint SHALL record its strategy — `image-content-hash-v1` for a photo, `video-md5-v1` for a video — and a
photo's the ImageMagick version that took it; a cached photo fingerprint is reused when both match the build's, a video's
when its strategy does.
sections: Prep — how this build does it
BLD-fingerprint_method.title: A fingerprint records its method

BLD-folder_fallback_cell.content:
Destinations SHALL be built parent first; each one's `folder_fallback` proposes, as `inherited` with `inherited_from`,
the `effective_fallback` of its nearest ancestor that has one, else `manual_required`. Its `effective_fallback` is the
`fallback_lat`/`fallback_lon` written there, else the inherited proposal when `accept_proposal` is true, else none; an
accepted proposal that does not exist is `stale_user_decision`. Its `requires_user_input` is always false.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-folder_fallback_cell.title: The folder-fallback cell

BLD-folder_removals.content:
Prep's plan SHALL end with an `rmdir` for each folder it leaves holding no file — under `0-sources`,
`4-videos-by-date` and `5-photos-by-date`, and on the first run the dump's own top-level folders — found by replaying
its moves over the files on disk, hidden ones included, deepest folder first; execute removes one only if it is then
empty, journals a folder found not empty or not removable as skipped, and warns of it.
sections: Prep — how this build does it
BLD-folder_removals.title: Folder removals are `rmdir` operations

BLD-format_recorded.content:
The handoff SHALL record the format prep named the files in as `filename_timestamp_format`; prep compares it with the
configured format at plan once a file outside the inbox carries a timestamp name, and geotag and merge at their start.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-format_recorded.title: The format recorded in the handoff

BLD-geotag_auto_reprep.content:
When the only change prep has not recorded is one {need}`BLD-reprep_pending` names and the inbox is empty, `geotag
plan` SHALL run prep's `plan` and `execute` itself, inside its own lock, saying so, before it plans.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-geotag_auto_reprep.title: Geotag runs prep itself when the inbox is empty

BLD-geotag_checks_decisions.content:
Geotag SHALL check the decisions in `photos-21`, `photos-22` and `photos-23` as it reads them (geotag §9.2, §20): each
blocker names the artifact, the destination, the cell or the file, and the field, and an artifact holding one is left as
it is, its plan not written. A decision artifact that cannot be read, does not parse as JSON or is not a JSON object is
such a blocker, located to where parsing failed — never taken as absent.
BLD-geotag_checks_decisions.section_name: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
sections: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-geotag_checks_decisions.title: Where geotag checks the decisions

BLD-geotag_dependencies.content:
`photos-24-executable-plan.json` SHALL record in `depends_on` the SHA-256 of `photos-21`, `photos-22` and `photos-23`;
the handoff's `content_fingerprint`; `config_fingerprint`, `code_fingerprint`, `camera_group_fingerprint`,
`camera_group_key_version`, `gpx_fingerprint`, `metadata_field_set_version`, `filename_format_fingerprint`,
`folders_fingerprint` and `media_extensions_fingerprint`; `resolved_utc_cache_fingerprint` and
`prep_cache_fingerprint`; each photo's `media_preconditions`; and `planned_operation_fingerprint`. Execute recomputes
all but the two cache fingerprints — vouched for by the records and handoff they were derived from, checked where they
are made — before any change, and each photo's preconditions as it applies it. `photos-25-execution-summary.json` is
never checked as a dependency.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-geotag_dependencies.title: Geotag's dependencies, recorded and checked

BLD-geotag_destinations.content:
A photo's destination SHALL be the `dirname` of its path; the container destinations are every ancestor of a
destination within `6-photos-by-dest` that is not one, `6-photos-by-dest` included, each marked `file_less: true` in the
decision records, its timezone and fallback cells never requiring input and its `camera_group_time_decisions` empty;
destinations are processed parents first.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-geotag_destinations.title: Geotag's destinations

BLD-geotag_execution.aliases: geotag-journal-every-op-1, geotag-reject-stale-before-mutation-1, geotag-execute-noclobber-recheck-1, geotag-prestate-before-write-1, geotag-tool-failure-not-silent-1, geotag-atomic-ops-1, geotag-snapshot-phase-label-1, geotag-snapshot-required-abort-1, geotag-concurrency-determinism-1, geotag-deterministic-aggregation-1, geotag-no-concurrent-decision-1, geotag-single-writer-1, geotag-no-partial-persistence-1
BLD-geotag_execution.content:
`geotag execute` SHALL, under the workspace lock: revalidate every dependency of photos-24 and stop before any change if
one moved; keep photos-21, -22 and -23 in `executed/<plan id>/`; take the snapshot labelled `geotag`, a required one
that fails ending the run as `rejected`; pin and move the own values, single-threaded; then, per photo and under
`-j`, skip one whose operations the journal confirms, find one renamed already by its target in place, and for one whose
size or modification time changed since the plan block if its decoded content differs and is not accepted, else read
its tags back — holding the planned values it is counted applied, otherwise, or with only a rename planned, it blocks
as edited since the plan. Otherwise it writes the photo's tags in one `exiftool -overwrite_original` call, retakes its
fingerprint — a changed one, not accepted, a mismatch that holds the photo's writes and rename back — and renames it,
the target checked free. The results merge in path order into the journal, kept per plan id, and photos-25.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-geotag_execution.title: How execution applies the plan

BLD-geotag_failed_write.content:
Geotag SHALL record a metadata write whose tool failed, or a rename that raised, as failed, confirming neither: a
failed write leaves the file as exiftool found it, a failed rename leaves it under its name.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-geotag_failed_write.title: Geotag's failed write

BLD-geotag_file_model.content:
Geotag's `build_file_model` SHALL take, from the handoff, only the records whose `folder_class` is `6-photos-by-dest`
and whose `media_class` is `image` or `raw`; every operation of `photos-24-executable-plan.json` names one of them.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-geotag_file_model.title: Geotag's file model

BLD-geotag_final_name.content:
Geotag SHALL compute the final name as resolved UTC → the destination's civil timezone → a local naive datetime → the
format.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-geotag_final_name.title: Geotag's final name, step by step

BLD-geotag_log_steps.content:
Geotag's steps SHALL be `clock_offset_applied` (its `offset_seconds` with an `offset_description` in words, such as
"camera clock 1 h 55 min ahead of UTC"), `resolved_utc`, `timezone_resolved`, `time_written`, `gps_written` (with its
origin, method and, for a manual position, the position it replaced, from the plan), `gps_cleared` (a position geotag
wrote and no longer places, with that position, from the plan, and the method left), `gps_preserved` and `final_rename`,
each naming its `run`; finalize takes them from every executed pass — each superseded `photos-24` whose journal shows it
ran, oldest first, matched by fingerprint — before the current plan's, from the provenance each time write carries
(geotag §31).
BLD-geotag_log_steps.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-geotag_log_steps.title: Geotag's steps in the log

BLD-geotag_records_by_destination.content:
`photos-21`, `photos-22`, `photos-23` and `photos-24` SHALL each hold a `destinations` object keyed by the
destination's path under `6-photos-by-dest`, every decision of a destination inside its entry.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-geotag_records_by_destination.title: Geotag's records are grouped by destination

BLD-geotag_stage_order.content:
`geotag plan` SHALL recognise the camera groups — stopping on an unknown one before reading any track — then read the
tracks, then write `photos-21-time-decisions.json`; only once it is complete resolve each photo's true time and
write `photos-22-gps-drift-validation.json`; only once that is complete write `photos-23-gps-decisions.json`; and only
once all three are complete assemble `photos-24-executable-plan.json`, which refuses any photo without a valid
resolved time.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-geotag_stage_order.title: Geotag's planning stages, in order

BLD-geotag_untimed_gate.content:
Geotag's preflight for `plan` SHALL block on every handoff record of a photo under `6-photos-by-dest` whose
`metadata_status.has_timestamp` — or, failing it, the `has_timestamp` of its `parsed_json` — is false, naming the
photos and `2-missing-metadata`.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-geotag_untimed_gate.title: Geotag's preflight refuses a photo with no recorded time

BLD-gps_decisions_record.content:
Each destination's entry in `photos-23-gps-decisions.json` SHALL hold its `folder_fallback` cell and `gps_decisions`:
a `summary` counting `files_total`, `preserve_native_gps`, `automatic_gpx_interpolation`,
`automatic_gpx_extrapolation`, `automatic_folder_fallback`, `manual_locked`, `no_gps_change_needed`, `blocked` and
`manual_review_required`; an `automatic_decision_summary` naming the track files used; and `review_items` — one per
photo `blocked` (`no_reliable_gps_source`, requiring input), `manual_locked` or `no_change` (`accepted_unlocated`),
each with `manual_lat`, `manual_lon` and `accept_unlocated`. No other photo is named: the executable plan derives every
automatic position again from its own inputs.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-gps_decisions_record.title: The GPS decisions record

BLD-gpx_fingerprint.content:
The GPX fingerprint SHALL be a SHA-256 over the resolved `gpx_root`, a version tag, and, in sorted order, each `*.gpx`
file's path relative to the root and the SHA-256 of its bytes, then every point read from them, in time order. An empty `gpx_root`, and a `gpx_root` that is not a
directory, each give a fixed value of their own, the second with a warning. It is recorded as `gpx_fingerprint` in the
`depends_on` of `photos-21-time-decisions.json`, `photos-22-gps-drift-validation.json`, `photos-23-gps-decisions.json`
and `photos-24-executable-plan.json`, and checked before each is used.
BLD-gpx_fingerprint.section_name: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
sections: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-gpx_fingerprint.title: The GPX fingerprint

BLD-gpx_root.content:
The tracks' location SHALL be the configuration key `gpx_root`: a path, absolute or relative to the workspace, resolved
through links before use; empty means no tracks. It MAY be anywhere outside `0-sources` … `6-photos-by-dest` — on any
disk, or under the control directory, such as `.photos-ingest/gpx/`, which prep's skip of `.photos-ingest/` already keeps
out of the scan. Geotag reads every `*.gpx` file beneath it. The value and the matching thresholds are read by geotag;
their detail is geotag §15 and §19.
BLD-gpx_root.section_name: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
sections: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-gpx_root.title: `gpx_root`

BLD-gpx_root_checked.content:
Configuration validation, in every phase, SHALL resolve `gpx_root` against the workspace, through links, and refuse it
when it is a managed folder, lies inside one, or contains one — the workspace root among them.
BLD-gpx_root_checked.section_name: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
sections: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-gpx_root_checked.title: `gpx_root` checked against the managed folders

BLD-handoff_content.content:
Prep's execute SHALL write `photos-11-handoff.json` last but for the database image and the mark, through a temporary
file renamed over it, holding: `schema_version`, `tool`, `run_metadata` (plan and execution ids), `cache_fingerprint`,
`folders_scanned` (the managed folders but `1-strays`, each with whether prep may change it), `files` (sorted, each with
its path, size, `mtime_ns`, media class, fingerprint and its status, folder and metadata),
`filename_timestamp_format`, `camera_groups`, `destination_folders` ({need}`BLD-handoff_grouping_facts`),
`diagnostics` (duplicates, blockers, warnings, quarantine footprint), `depends_on` (configuration, prep log, journal,
final inventory, metadata extractor, plan and database versions, image engine) and `content_fingerprint`.
sections: Prep — how this build does it
BLD-handoff_content.title: What the handoff holds

BLD-handoff_content_fingerprint.content:
`content_fingerprint` SHALL be the SHA-256 of the handoff serialized with sorted keys, without the keys `run_metadata`,
`diagnostics`, `execution_journal`, `prep_log`, `content_fingerprint`, `cache_freshness` and `conflicts_or_duplicates`
wherever they appear — the last two being each camera group's and destination folder's run-scoped counts and
duplicates.
sections: Prep — how this build does it
BLD-handoff_content_fingerprint.title: The handoff's content fingerprint

BLD-handoff_grouping_facts.content:
The handoff SHALL carry `camera_groups` — each group's key, files and count, identity fields, earliest and latest
recorded time, native-GPS, missing-GPS and missing-time counts, cache freshness and the device class the configuration
gives it — and `destination_folders` — each folder's path, files scanned, camera groups, time range, native-GPS,
missing-GPS and `GPSProcessingMethod` counts, cache freshness, and the duplicates whose kept copy it holds.
BLD-handoff_grouping_facts.section_name: 12. The metadata prep keeps for geotag
sections: 12. The metadata prep keeps for geotag
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-handoff_grouping_facts.title: The handoff's camera groups and destination folders

BLD-handoff_hashes.content:
The handoff SHALL be `photos-11-handoff.json` in `.photos-ingest/`, which geotag checks by its `content_fingerprint` —
the content-scoped staleness key prep stamps on it ({need}`BLD-handoff_content_fingerprint`) — recomputing it and comparing it with the value in
geotag's dependency block (geotag §4). Its whole-file SHA-256 is kept as an integrity and archival hash ({need}`DEF-archival_package`),
never the dependency check.
BLD-handoff_hashes.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-handoff_hashes.title: The handoff's two hashes

BLD-hash.content: A hash SHALL be a SHA-256 over the exact bytes of a numbered JSON record or the configuration.
BLD-hash.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-hash.title: How a hash is computed

BLD-history_kept.content:
Each run's journal SHALL be kept as its own `journal-<run>.json`, each geotag execution keeping the decision records its
plan depended on, verified by hash, in `executed/<plan id>/`, which a step's `because_record` and
`because_record_sha256` name.
BLD-history_kept.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-history_kept.title: The journals and the decisions each execution used are kept

BLD-idempotency.content:
Each phase SHALL reuse what is still valid: prep, the cached fingerprint and metadata of a file whose size and
modification time are unchanged, carrying a moved file's identity forward without reading it ({need}`RUL-moved_file_carried`), a plan never executed leaving its fingerprints and metadata for the next plan to reuse
({need}`RUL-plan_memo_kept`); geotag reads no photo,
taking every photo's metadata from prep, works out its results again on each run — a result that comes out the same
leaving everything that depends on it as it is — keeps each decision whose target is unchanged (geotag §9, §22.1), and
reads every track file whole for its fingerprint but parses only one whose bytes it has not parsed before, taking the
rest from its track memo, `photos-00-track-memo.db`; merge, a library file's fingerprint while its size and
modification time are unchanged (merge §7). Fingerprinting (ImageMagick `identify`, `ffmpeg`), metadata extraction
(`exiftool`) and GPX parsing thus run only for new or changed inputs. Each phase's own consequences are in its spec:
{need}`RUL-no_op_run` and prep §21, geotag §29.1 and §30, merge §8.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-idempotency.title: What each phase reuses

BLD-identical_replan_writes_nothing.content: A re-plan whose content is byte-identical to the saved artifact SHALL write nothing and back up nothing.
BLD-identical_replan_writes_nothing.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-identical_replan_writes_nothing.title: A byte-identical re-plan writes nothing

BLD-init_library_cases.content:
`merge init-library [path]` SHALL resolve a given path to an absolute one and require an existing directory, then:
inside a workspace with a path, refuse a path `library_place_error` names and, under the lock, check the workspace's
filesystem and the seal, read the configuration through `load_config`, mark the directory and record it as
`merge.library_root`; inside a workspace without one, under the lock, read the configuration the same way and mark the
`library_root` it names, writing nothing in the workspace; outside any workspace with a path, mark the directory and
write nothing else; outside any workspace without one, stop with exit status 2. A configuration that cannot be read or
fails its checks stops it with exit status 2, nothing marked and nothing written.
sections: Merge — how this build does it
BLD-init_library_cases.title: `init-library`'s four cases

BLD-init_library_checks_seal.content:
`merge init-library` given a path from inside a workspace, which would record it as `library_root` in the configuration,
SHALL check the seal under the lock the same way, and stop with exit status 2 having blessed nothing; without a path, or
from outside any workspace, it writes nothing in the workspace and does not check.
BLD-init_library_checks_seal.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-init_library_checks_seal.title: `init-library` checks the seal before recording a library

BLD-init_library_writes_library_root.content:
The setup command `init-library` (merge §4), run inside a workspace with an explicit library path, MAY write the
`library_root` key into the configuration, and only that key. It is not part of merge's data path.
BLD-init_library_writes_library_root.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-init_library_writes_library_root.title: `init-library` may write `library_root`

BLD-job_records_kept.content:
Each phase's job records — prep's handoff and summary, geotag's decision, plan and execution-summary records, merge's
summary — SHALL stay on disk, as do every pass's plan and journal and the decision records each execution kept
(`BLD-log_format`).
BLD-job_records_kept.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-job_records_kept.title: The job records stay on disk

BLD-jpeg_extensions.content:
A JPEG SHALL be a file of the `image` class ending `.jpg` or `.jpeg`, matched ignoring case; a raw file, one of the
`raw` class.
sections: Prep — how this build does it
BLD-jpeg_extensions.title: What counts as a JPEG and a raw file

BLD-known_camera_group.content:
A group SHALL be known when its key is listed under `camera_time_and_timezone_policy.device_groups` — `phones` (mobile)
or `fixed_clock_cameras` (fixed-clock).
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-known_camera_group.title: A camera group is known when it is listed

BLD-library_file_fingerprinted.content:
Where a file is there, merge SHALL fingerprint it — from `library_fingerprint_cache` when its path, size and
modification time match a row taken by this build's photo method under the current, known ImageMagick version,
otherwise by decoding it and storing the row — and compare it with the incoming photo's fingerprint from prep. A file
whose name differs from the target's only in case is such a file: the same content is already present at its name.
Only planning writes these rows; execute fingerprints afresh and writes no row.
BLD-library_file_fingerprinted.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-library_file_fingerprinted.title: A library file in the way is fingerprinted, through a cache

BLD-library_folders_made.content: Merge SHALL create a missing destination directory under `library_root` with `os.makedirs` as it places a photo there.
BLD-library_folders_made.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-library_folders_made.title: Merge makes a destination's folder as it places a photo

BLD-library_lock.content:
The library lock SHALL be `LibraryLock`: an exclusive, non-blocking `flock` on `.photos-merge.lock` in `library_root`,
recording its holder's `pid`, `started_at` and `host` and nothing else, released by the kernel when its process dies,
the file never deleted; merge's `plan`, `dry-run` and `execute` take it after the workspace lock and after the
preflight's `validate_merge_config` and `is_library` checks, and hold it to their end, one that cannot take it stopping
with exit status 1.
BLD-library_lock.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-library_lock.title: The library lock

BLD-library_marker.content:
A library SHALL be marked by an empty `.photos-library` file in `library_root`, which `is_library` tests with
`os.path.isfile` and `merge init-library` alone creates, with `O_CREAT|O_EXCL`, leaving one already there as it is
(merge §4).
BLD-library_marker.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-library_marker.title: The library's mark

BLD-library_root_validated.content:
`validate_merge_config` SHALL require `merge.library_root` to be non-empty and to resolve to an existing directory that
is neither the workspace nor inside it.
BLD-library_root_validated.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-library_root_validated.title: `validate_merge_config` checks the library's place

BLD-lock_after_guard.content:
The lock SHALL be taken as soon as the run's workspace is known, before the guard, `photos-00-workspace-guard`, or
anything else in it is read.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-lock_after_guard.title: The lock is taken first

BLD-lock_owner_record.content:
The lock SHALL record the identity of the process that owns it and the time it started, so that a lock whose owner is
gone can be told from one whose owner is running.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-lock_owner_record.title: The lock records its owner

BLD-log_copy_checked.content:
Each copy SHALL carry the earlier log unchanged — every entry, every field and every step as it was, a phase only adding
— which finalize and merge check: a copy that would change the earlier record is not written, and merge refuses while
`photos-26-complete-log.json` no longer carries `photos-15-prep-log.json` so, or cannot be read.
BLD-log_copy_checked.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-log_copy_checked.title: A copied log carries the earlier one unchanged

BLD-log_format.content:
Each log SHALL be pretty-printed JSON with sorted keys, its `photos` keyed by the content fingerprint
(`content_fingerprint`), each entry carrying where each phase left the photo — `prep_path`, written by prep and updated
by every prep run; `geotag_path`, by finalize, its by-dest folder under the name its last final rename gave it;
`library_path`, by merge — and a `journey` of steps, each step naming its `phase` and `action`, a move or rename its
`from` and `to` — the first step's `from` being the photo's path in the dump — and, where a decision caused it, a
`because` naming the decision exactly: a clock offset its `photos-21` cell, with its day where the camera's photos there
span days (`camera_group_time_decisions.<group>@<date>`), or the `photos-22` drift confirmation whose validated offset
replaced it; a timezone its destination's cell; a manual position the photo's pin among `photos-23`'s review items or
the destination's folder fallback, with the destination it was accepted from.
BLD-log_format.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-log_format.title: The log's format

BLD-loop_commands.content:
The loop SHALL run as: `prep plan`, `dry-run`, `execute`; the sort, by hand; the prep commands again; `geotag plan`, the
decision editor (`edit`) for what it asks, and `geotag plan` again until `photos-24-executable-plan.json` is ready;
`geotag execute`, which writes `photos-25-execution-summary.json`; `geotag finalize`, which writes
`photos-26-complete-log.json` and the archival package; and `merge plan`, `dry-run`, `execute`.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-loop_commands.title: The loop's commands

BLD-loop_gates.content:
The gates SHALL be checked as follows: `geotag plan` checks every gate; `geotag execute` and `finalize` check the
development gate and the workspace's shape, and validate against the plan's own dependencies instead of the scope and
re-prep gates (geotag §7, §13.1); merge's preflight checks the inbox, the development gate and that photos by
destination holds only photos (merge §3). A development subfolder is one named in `destination_distribution_subfolders`.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-loop_gates.title: Where the loop's gates are checked

BLD-marked_file_rerun.content:
On a re-run, a file with no pinned values carrying a position marker or the suffix SHALL be resolved from its own time
and offset tag with no clock offset, as no clock anchor and in no drift check, a camera group's offset cells being built
from its unmarked files alone. A file with a position marker counts as having no native GPS and is placed again; one now
placed nowhere has geotag's position and marker cleared and carries the suffix alone.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-marked_file_rerun.title: A re-run treats a marked file as geotag's work

BLD-merge_carry_forward.content:
Merge's `build_merge_plan` SHALL give a finalized photo no longer under `6-photos-by-dest` the record of the latest
plan — `photos-30-merge-plan.json`, then its `-NNN` backups newest first — holding a record for its content fingerprint
not blocked whose `library_target` fingerprints, through `_fingerprint_library_file`, to it, adding `carried_from_plan`
(the plan that first placed it); no such record makes it a blocked record whose reason names the places tried, or that
no earlier plan placed it.
sections: Merge — how this build does it
BLD-merge_carry_forward.title: A fresh plan carries forward from the earlier plans

BLD-merge_collision.content:
Merge SHALL map each photo by destination to its place under `library_root`, and list only the folders its photos go to
— for the names taken there — and the library's top folder, for temporary copies a crash of its own left (§15).
BLD-merge_collision.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-merge_collision.title: Where merge looks in the library

BLD-merge_engine_recheck.content:
Merge's plan SHALL compare the ImageMagick version now in use with the handoff's `depends_on.cache.image_engine_version`
— a handoff recording none counting as another — and, where they differ and the current one is known, fingerprint each
by-dest photo it plans to place, blocking one whose value is not the handoff's; the plan records the version in its
`depends_on.image_engine_version`, and a plan made under another is stale, at dry run and execute alike.
sections: Merge — how this build does it
BLD-merge_engine_recheck.title: Merge checks prep's fingerprints against the handoff's ImageMagick

BLD-merge_execute.content:
Merge's execute SHALL, on its main thread, revalidate the plan's `depends_on`, take the snapshots and sweep the
temporaries a crash left; then move the photos on a pool of `jobs` workers, each touching only its own photo and
returning a result; the main thread alone writing the journal, as each result arrives, and sorting the results by path
before the summary is built.
sections: Merge — how this build does it
BLD-merge_execute.title: Merge's execute, in order

BLD-merge_failed_placement.content: Merge SHALL record a placement that raised as blocked, its photo left in photos by destination.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-merge_failed_placement.title: Merge's failed placement

BLD-merge_journal_resume.content:
The journal SHALL record each confirmed photo, a re-run taking a place already holding the planned content,
fingerprinted again, as done, and removing the workspace copy if it remains; a photo whose workspace copy is gone, the
journal confirming it or the plan finding it already present, counts as done only once its place is fingerprinted again
and found to hold it, and is blocked otherwise.
BLD-merge_journal_resume.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-merge_journal_resume.title: Merge's journal, and how a re-run resumes

BLD-merge_move.content:
Each photo SHALL move into its place without overwriting it: on the library's own filesystem by a single rename that
refuses an existing name; across filesystems by a copy to a temporary name beside its place, checked byte for byte against
the photo, renamed into the place only if it is still free, the rename made durable, and only then removed from photos
by destination.
A place found taken at execute holding the planned content makes the photo already present; holding other content, it
blocks the photo — the plan's alternative name used only where the plan recorded one.
BLD-merge_move.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-merge_move.title: Merge's move: one rename, or copy, verify, rename and remove

BLD-merge_plan.content:
`photos-30-merge-plan.json` SHALL hold the plan id, schema version and `library_root`; per destination, each photo's
record — its path in the workspace, content fingerprint, library target and disposition (`placed_new`,
`renamed_incoming` with its new name, `already_present`, or `blocked` with why), and as preconditions its fingerprint
and its size and modification time as they stand at planning; the blockers and the totals; and `depends_on`: the
SHA-256 of `photos-24` and `photos-25`, the handoff's content fingerprint, the configuration's SHA-256, the code
fingerprint, the ImageMagick version, and the fingerprints of the folder names and media extensions.
sections: Merge — how this build does it
BLD-merge_plan.title: Merge's plan

BLD-merge_preflight.content:
Merge's `preflight` SHALL run, under the workspace lock and before the library's, stopping at the first that fails:
the seal; the initialization mark; a link at the top level; a missing managed folder; a misplaced top-level entry; the
configuration, read and checked; the library's place and mark; the handoff, read; its filename format. It then gathers
the rest and reports them together: the inbox empty; `photos-24-executable-plan.json` present with
`photos-25-execution-summary.json` at `success`; the handoff's content fingerprint the one `photos-24` pinned; prep's
log as the handoff vouches for it ({need}`BLD-prep_log_checked`); `photos-26-complete-log.json` and the archive
manifest present, the complete log carrying prep's; photos by date holding no photo; photos by destination holding
only `image` and `raw` files, no development subfolder and no link; every photo there one of the finalized set — the
handoff's photos by destination joined by fingerprint to `photos-24`'s renames, each under its final name; and each
photo of that set still there with the size and modification time `photos-26-finalized-media.json` recorded. Any
blocker ends the run with exit status 2 before the library lock, the plan or the summary.
sections: Merge — how this build does it
BLD-merge_preflight.title: Merge's preflight

BLD-merge_records.content:
Merge SHALL write `photos-31-merge-summary.json` on every outcome but a stale plan or a failed precondition: per photo,
grouped by destination, where it landed, whether it was renamed for the library or already present, whether it left
photos by destination, and, blocked, why — with no library path; in total, the photos placed new, renamed, already
present and blocked, the removed the sum of the first three; the status `success`, `partial`, `failed` (every photo
blocked) or `rejected` (a required snapshot not taken, nothing changed); the merge run and plan ids, `library_root`, the
geotag plan and execution ids, the photos it newly moved and those an earlier run had, and the SHA-256 of `photos-24-executable-plan.json`,
`photos-25-execution-summary.json` and `photos-11-handoff.json`; and, apart, the run's times and job count.
BLD-merge_records.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-merge_records.title: The merge summary

BLD-merge_snapshots.content:
Merge's `_take_snapshots` SHALL snapshot the workspace's dataset and then, where the library's differs, the library's —
each pinned by `zfs.datasets.workspace` and `zfs.datasets.library` or detected from its path — taking the library's
only after the workspace's has succeeded, and recording both in `photos-31-merge-summary.json` under `snapshot`.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-merge_snapshots.title: Merge's two snapshots

BLD-merge_success_sequence.content:
Only on success — every photo placed or already present, none left — SHALL merge then, in order, write
`photos-35-merge-log.json`, `photos-35-merge-ingest.db`, the package's `photos-35-archive-manifest.json` and
`photos-35-archive.tar.gz`, and last the seal.
BLD-merge_success_sequence.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-merge_success_sequence.title: What a whole merge writes, and the seal last

BLD-merge_target.content:
Merge's `enumerate_finalized` SHALL take each photo of the handoff under `6-photos-by-dest` and give it, as its target,
`library_root` joined to its folder's path relative to `6-photos-by-dest` — empty for a photo directly in it — and its
final name: the target of `photos-24`'s `rename_no_clobber` whose `content_fingerprint` precondition is the photo's, or
its own name where geotag renamed nothing; the entries sorted by their path in the workspace.
sections: Merge — how this build does it
BLD-merge_target.title: A photo's target in the library

BLD-metadata_extraction.content:
Prep SHALL read metadata with `exiftool -json -n -a -G0`, taking each field from the first group holding it in the
order `EXIF`, `XMP`, `MakerNotes`, `IPTC`, `QuickTime`, `File` — `Composite` first for the GPS position — and a time
field from the first group holding a valid time in it; it keeps the fields in `metadata_cache.parsed_json` with the
recorded time's field and group, stamped with `exiftool`, its version, the field-set version, the SHA-256 of the
options, the metadata-schema version and the camera-group-key version.
BLD-metadata_extraction.section_name: 12. The metadata prep keeps for geotag
sections: 12. The metadata prep keeps for geotag
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-metadata_extraction.title: Metadata is read by exiftool, by group

BLD-metadata_safe_write.content:
Geotag SHALL write metadata with `exiftool -overwrite_original`, which writes a temporary file and renames it over the
original, having first removed a `<file>_exiftool_tmp` an interrupted write left (geotag §29.1a).
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-metadata_safe_write.title: Geotag's metadata writes

BLD-move_match.content:
Prep's plan SHALL match, before laying the plan memo under the database, the rows of the workspace database whose path
is not in the inventory against the inventoried files under `6-photos-by-dest` that have no row, by size, `mtime_ns`
and exact basename; a triple held by more than one row or more than one file matches nothing.
BLD-move_match.section_name: 10. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
sections: 10. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-move_match.title: The move is matched on size, time and name

BLD-move_row_effects.content:
Each move or rename in prep's plan SHALL carry its database effects — the row of its source removed and, but for a
quarantine move, the file's row with its fingerprint and metadata written at its destination — applied by execute once
the operation succeeds.
BLD-move_row_effects.section_name: 10. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
sections: 10. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-move_row_effects.title: A planned move carries its row

BLD-name_check.content:
At plan, prep SHALL check the name of every media file in the dated, missing-metadata, redundant-JPG and by-destination
folders: without its extension and `-NNN` suffix, it is the file's recorded time ({need}`RUL-recorded_time_order`)
formatted by `filename_timestamp_format`, or starts with `UNKN_` for a file with no recorded time and for every file in
the missing-metadata folder. A dated file with no recorded time is moved to the missing-metadata folder instead, and the
strays folder is not checked.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-name_check.title: What prep checks a name against

BLD-name_suffix.content:
The names SHALL be `<timestamp>.ext` for the first file with a free base name, `<timestamp>-001.ext` for the first
collision, `<timestamp>-002.ext` for the second, and so on.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-name_suffix.title: The `-NNN` suffix

BLD-no_clobber_rename.content:
Every move and rename that carries content SHALL go through `_move_no_clobber`: on one filesystem `renameat2` with
`RENAME_NOREPLACE`, one call that refuses an existing name, or where that is unavailable `os.link` then `os.unlink`;
across filesystems, for merge alone, `_move_cross_fs_no_clobber`. A refused name stops that operation: prep records it
failed and stops; geotag and merge record a blocker and leave the photo where it is. Merge also tests its target before
moving, and geotag compares names ignoring case (geotag §27). The rename that completes an operation is thus itself the
check that its name is free ({need}`RUL-target_free_at_execute`; geotag §29.1a, merge §11).
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-no_clobber_rename.title: One rename that refuses a taken name

BLD-no_control_dir_stops.content:
Geotag and merge SHALL check that the control directory exists before they take the lock, and where it does not, stop
with exit status 2, having created nothing.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-no_control_dir_stops.title: Geotag and merge stop where there is no control directory

BLD-offset_buckets.content:
Each destination's `camera_group_time_decisions` SHALL hold one cell per camera group present, keyed by its
`camera_group_key`, or — when the group's photos there span more than one naive date — one per date, keyed
`<camera_group_key>@<YYYY-MM-DD>` with a `date` field, the date taken from `source_naive_time`. A cell's proposal is
the GPX self-anchor of that group's native-GPS frames of that date there; else, with the destination's timezone
resolved, `timezone_naive` at the cell's earliest naive time, DST-aware; else `manual_required`. No cell reads another
destination's.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-offset_buckets.title: Offset buckets

BLD-one_snapshot_mechanism.content:
The three phases SHALL take their snapshots through one mechanism — prep's execute, geotag §29 and merge §10.3 invoke it,
and none redefines it.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-one_snapshot_mechanism.title: One snapshot mechanism for every phase

BLD-one_top_level_check.content:
Prep, geotag and merge SHALL find a workspace's misplaced top-level entries with the one function they share,
`photos_utils.misplaced_top_level_entries`, so the three cannot disagree on what belongs there.
BLD-one_top_level_check.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-one_top_level_check.title: One check of the top level for all three phases

BLD-operation_only_where_different.content:
A file's operation SHALL be planned only where the file does not already hold the target: prep does not move or rename a
file already in place, geotag plans no write a file already holds and recomputes an already-final name to itself (geotag
§27, §28.2), and merge records a photo already in the library as already present (merge §7).
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-operation_only_where_different.title: An operation only where the file differs

BLD-original_values_follow_fingerprint.content:
`build_file_model` SHALL find a photo's pinned values under its fingerprint or, failing it, under the value it was
taken again from, step by step back through the `fingerprint_retaken` steps of prep's log (`retaken_fingerprints`),
when the handoff vouches for the log; execution then moves the pin to the current value, unless one is held there. A
log holding two steps that give one value two predecessors, or one value two successors, is a blocker of geotag's
preflight.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-original_values_follow_fingerprint.title: The pinned values follow a retaken fingerprint

BLD-original_values_pinned.content:
Before geotag's first write to a file, execution SHALL pin its own time, offset tag, position and `GPSProcessingMethod`
in an original-values ledger keyed by fingerprint, once, unless it already carries geotag's mark; a later plan decides
about a pinned file from those values and plans only the writes that differ from what it holds (geotag §24.2).
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-original_values_pinned.title: A file's own values are pinned before geotag first writes it

BLD-partial_log_marked.content:
A log whose kept history cannot rebuild a journey SHALL be marked partial: prep marks its log partial and warns when its
history cannot rebuild a journey ({need}`BLD-prep_log_build`); geotag's finalize marks `partial` the entry of a photo carrying geotag's
mark whose own values the workspace never pinned, with a `history_incomplete` step of its own saying why, and names in
the log's `warnings`, the log then `partial`, any pass whose journal is kept but whose plan is missing (geotag §31).
BLD-partial_log_marked.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-partial_log_marked.title: A log that cannot rebuild a journey is marked partial

BLD-phase_commands.content:
The phases SHALL be the commands `photos-cartographer prep`, `geotag` and `merge` — named in the specs, and in their
records, `photos-1-prep`, `photos-2-geotag` and `photos-3-merge`.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-phase_commands.title: The phases are three commands

BLD-phase_dependencies.content:
Each phase SHALL record a record's dependencies in its `depends_on` block and check them before use, as its own spec
states in full: prep in {need}`BLD-prep_dependencies`; geotag in {need}`BLD-geotag_dependencies`; merge in {need}`BLD-merge_plan`. The cascade consumes media by content fingerprints, records by byte
hashes, and the field-scoped configuration fingerprints ({need}`DEF-config_areas`) that keep staleness surgical.
BLD-phase_dependencies.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-phase_dependencies.title: Each phase's dependencies, in full

BLD-phase_logs.content:
Each phase SHALL write its log: prep `photos-15-prep-log.json` at the end of every prep run ({need}`BLD-prep_log_build`); geotag's
finalize copies it to `photos-26-complete-log.json` and appends each photo's geotag steps (§13.3); merge copies that to
`photos-35-merge-log.json` and appends its own (§13.5).
BLD-phase_logs.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-phase_logs.title: The per-phase logs

BLD-phases_check_seal.content:
Prep's `plan`, `dry-run` and `execute`, every geotag command, and merge's `plan`, `dry-run` and `execute` SHALL check
the seal under the workspace lock before reading anything else, and stop with exit status 2 if it is there, adding the
likely-new-dump warning when `likely_new_dump` finds an entry at the workspace's top level other than its managed
folders and hidden entries, or anything in the inbox.
BLD-phases_check_seal.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-phases_check_seal.title: The phases check the seal first

BLD-phases_inside_lock.content:
Each phase's `plan`, `dry-run` and `execute` SHALL run with the lock taken at start already held, none taking it again
or scoping it on its own ({need}`RUL-lock_through_the_run`; geotag §29).
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-phases_inside_lock.title: The phases run inside the run's lock

BLD-placement_order.content:
`classify_gps` SHALL return, for each photo, the first of: `preserve_native` for a photo with its own position; its
review item's `manual_lat`/`manual_lon` as `manual_locked`; the tracks at its resolved time as `gpx_interpolation` or
`gpx_extrapolation`; its destination's effective fallback as `manual_fallback`; `no_change` for a photo marked
`accept_unlocated`; else `blocked`. A position from `manual_locked` or `manual_fallback` is written with that marker,
and undone like any manual position.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-placement_order.title: The placement order

BLD-plan_backups.content:
A differing re-plan SHALL first rename the existing artifact under the shared incremental `-NNN` suffix ({need}`BLD-name_suffix`) —
`photos-10-prep-plan-001.json`, say — and announce where. A plan carrying a fresh plan id differs every run, so
re-planning it always preserves the prior plan. The per-run journals keep their `journal-<run_id>.json` naming; this
convention governs the plan and decision artifacts.
BLD-plan_backups.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-plan_backups.title: A superseded plan goes aside under `-NNN`

BLD-plan_memo.content:
The plan memo SHALL be the SQLite file `photos-00-plan-memo.db` in `.photos-ingest/`, one row per path with its size,
`mtime_ns` and the file's row as read, replaced whole by each plan with its media files holding both a fingerprint and a
metadata record; read, its entries lie under the database's rows and pass the same reuse tests, and failing to open,
read or write it warns and goes on.
BLD-plan_memo.section_name: 10. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
sections: 10. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-plan_memo.title: The plan memo is `photos-00-plan-memo.db`

BLD-planned_paths_tracked.content:
Each stage of prep's planning SHALL work from the path the stages before it gave each file, allocating every name
against the names on disk and those already planned.
sections: Prep — how this build does it
BLD-planned_paths_tracked.title: Each stage works from the paths the stages before it planned

BLD-planning_order.content:
Prep SHALL walk the workspace and take its files' sizes and times on one thread, sorted, before any parallel work, and
gather the workers' results by path; two plans of one workspace differ only in `plan_id`, `created_at` and the
operations' ids.
BLD-planning_order.section_name: 17. Concurrency, determinism, and what a run shows
sections: 17. Concurrency, determinism, and what a run shows
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-planning_order.title: Planning in a fixed order

BLD-position_tags.content:
Every position geotag writes SHALL carry, in the same operation, `GPSLatitude`, `GPSLatitudeRef` (`N` or `S` by the
sign), `GPSLongitude` and `GPSLongitudeRef` (`E` or `W`); clearing one empties all four.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-position_tags.title: Position tags

BLD-prep_dependencies.content:
Prep's records SHALL carry their dependencies so:

- **The plan** records its schema version, the configuration's hash, its metadata dependencies — exiftool and its
  version, and the versions of the field set, the extraction options, the metadata schema and the camera-group
  derivation — and the size and mtime of every file it reads without changing, those in `6-photos-by-dest` among them.
  Execute recomputes each and refuses the plan when one differs or is absent.
- **The journal**'s `depends_on` records the plan's schema version, the configuration's hash, and the cache's schema and
  fingerprint-algorithm versions.
- **The handoff**'s `depends_on` records the configuration's hash, the metadata dependencies, the plan's and the cache's
  schema versions, the fingerprint algorithm and the image engine with its version, the journal's hash, the prep log's
  hash ({need}`BLD-prep_log_vouched`), and the fingerprint of the final inventory.
- **The workspace database** records its schema and fingerprint-algorithm versions in its `meta` table.

A run's inventory and freshness maps are its own working state, recorded nowhere. No command option affects what prep
plans, so no record carries one.
BLD-prep_dependencies.section_name: 5. What each of prep’s records depends on
sections: 5. What each of prep’s records depends on
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-prep_dependencies.title: Prep's dependencies, in full

BLD-prep_execute_replays.content:
Prep's execute SHALL apply the operations of `photos-10-prep-plan.json` in their recorded order, to the destinations
recorded there, running no step of planning.
BLD-prep_execute_replays.section_name: 4. The plan, validated, then carried out
sections: 4. The plan, validated, then carried out
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-prep_execute_replays.title: Prep's execute replays the saved plan

BLD-prep_fast_stop_checks_log.content:
Prep's stop on an already-prepped workspace SHALL not apply while the log's hash differs from what the handoff records,
so that prep's next execute rewrites both.
BLD-prep_fast_stop_checks_log.section_name: 5. What each of prep’s records depends on
sections: 5. What each of prep’s records depends on
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-prep_fast_stop_checks_log.title: A log not vouched for is not "nothing to do"

BLD-prep_guards_with_the_whole_hash.content:
Prep SHALL re-plan from the filesystem each run and guard execution with the whole-file hash, keeping no folder or
extension fingerprint of its own.
BLD-prep_guards_with_the_whole_hash.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-prep_guards_with_the_whole_hash.title: Prep guards execution with the whole-file hash

BLD-prep_journal.content:
Prep's execute SHALL append each operation's outcome to `journal-<plan-id>.json` as the operation ends, saving the
journal after each by replacing it whole — written to a temporary file in its folder, then renamed over it.
BLD-prep_journal.section_name: 4. The plan, validated, then carried out
sections: 4. The plan, validated, then carried out
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-prep_journal.title: Prep journals each operation as it ends

BLD-prep_log_build.content:
Prep's execute SHALL build `photos-15-prep-log.json` from the plan's moves and renames replayed per file, the
quarantine evidence and the final database rows, merged onto the prior log by fingerprint: an entry whose old value is
nowhere in the workspace and whose `prep_path` holds a file of a new value moves to it with a `fingerprint_retaken`
step; an entry whose file is elsewhere with no step of this run gains a `user` step `moved_to_by_dest`; and a file in
a prep-organized folder with no recorded history gets an entry marked `partial`, with a warning.
sections: Prep — how this build does it
BLD-prep_log_build.title: How prep's log is built

BLD-prep_log_checked.content:
Finalize and merge SHALL stop while `photos-15-prep-log.json` is not the log the handoff vouches for
({need}`BLD-prep_log_vouched`) — missing, unreadable, its SHA-256 other than `depends_on.prep_log`'s, or the handoff
recording none — through the shared `prep_log_blocker`, merge among its gathered preconditions.
BLD-prep_log_checked.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-prep_log_checked.title: Prep's log is checked against the handoff

BLD-prep_log_vouched.content:
Prep's execute SHALL write `photos-15-prep-log.json` before the handoff, and record the log's SHA-256 in the handoff's
`depends_on.prep_log`, outside its content fingerprint.
BLD-prep_log_vouched.section_name: 5. What each of prep’s records depends on
sections: 5. What each of prep’s records depends on
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-prep_log_vouched.title: The handoff vouches for prep's log

BLD-prep_operation_kinds.content:
Prep's execute SHALL carry out only folder creations, moves, renames, quarantine moves and database writes, refusing a
plan that holds any other operation — a metadata write among them.
BLD-prep_operation_kinds.section_name: 2. What prep does, and what it leaves alone
sections: 2. What prep does, and what it leaves alone
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-prep_operation_kinds.title: Prep's operations hold no metadata write

BLD-prep_plan_contents.content:
`photos-10-prep-plan.json` SHALL record its id, its schema version, its command, the configuration's hash, the
fingerprint of the code that made it ({need}`BLD-code_fingerprint`), its operations in order, its blockers and warnings,
the size and modification time of each file it leaves as it is, its metadata dependencies, every path its scan found,
and a summary.
sections: Prep — how this build does it
BLD-prep_plan_contents.title: What prep's plan records

BLD-prep_skip_set.content:
Prep SHALL skip `.photos-ingest/`, `.photos-ingest-quarantine/` and `.git` as whole subtrees, every dot-prefixed file,
and the strays folder `1-strays/` with all its `<plan-id>` subfolders (prep §3, §3.2), the strays of a run going to
`1-strays/<plan-id>/`.
BLD-prep_skip_set.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-prep_skip_set.title: What prep skips

BLD-prep_stage_order.content:
Prep's planning SHALL run its stages in this order: initialization and inventory; duplicates; extension case; redundant
JPEGs; organization by class and time; database reconciliation.
sections: Prep — how this build does it
BLD-prep_stage_order.title: The stages run in a fixed order

BLD-prune_command.content:
`prep prune-quarantine` SHALL remove whole `<plan-id>` folders of the quarantine, selected by `--plan-id` (repeatable)
or `--older-than-days` — a run's age taken from the time in its plan id, the two selecting the runs either names —
listing them with their files and bytes and deleting only with `--yes`, and with no selector only with `--all` too; the
plan's summary carries the quarantine's footprint.
sections: Prep — how this build does it
BLD-prune_command.title: `prune-quarantine` and its selectors

BLD-prune_ignores_seal.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-prune_ignores_seal.title: `prune-quarantine` does not check the seal

BLD-quarantine_layout.content:
A quarantined file SHALL go to `.photos-ingest-quarantine/<plan-id>/` at its workspace path, its entry — original path,
quarantine path, the copy kept, the fingerprint and the plan id — appended to that folder's `manifest.json` before the
move; the manifest is replaced whole at each append, and one found unreadable is set aside as
`manifest.json.corrupt-<time>-<random>` and a new one begun.
sections: Prep — how this build does it
BLD-quarantine_layout.title: The quarantine's layout and manifest

BLD-record_ownership.content:
A phase SHALL write only records in its own number band of the numbering scheme: prep `photos-1X`, geotag `photos-2X`,
merge `photos-3X`, and on success the seal, `photos-00-sealed.json`, which merge alone writes. The configuration and
the database are phase-neutral, each with its own writers' rule: prep seeds
the configuration, which `init-library` may later extend by `library_root` alone (§4), and prep writes the database's
cache and identity rows while geotag and merge write only their own regions of it (§13.4). Bundling copies of every phase's records into the archival package reads them, and is no write.
BLD-record_ownership.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-record_ownership.title: Which phase writes which record

BLD-rehash_summary.content:
The plan's `performance_and_cache.rehash_summary` SHALL count the media files fingerprinted this run by reason — `new`,
`moved-unmatched`, `size-changed`, `mtime-changed`, `metadata-stale`, `failed-before`, `engine-changed` — with a sample
of the unexpected ones, and the fingerprints reused from the plan memo.
BLD-rehash_summary.section_name: 17. Concurrency, determinism, and what a run shows
sections: 17. Concurrency, determinism, and what a run shows
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-rehash_summary.title: The re-fingerprint summary

BLD-rename_planning.content:
For each destination, `plan_renames` SHALL count every current name of its photos as taken, case folded, and never
freed by a rename it plans — two photos that would trade names both take a suffix — then, in path order, leave a photo
whose name already carries its timestamp, suffix and all, as it is, and give any other the first free name of its
timestamp by `allocate_suffix`, adding it to the names taken. Execution applies these renames and no other, each by a
no-clobber move.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-rename_planning.title: How renames are planned

BLD-reprep_pending.content:
`by_dest_reprep_pending` SHALL name, from sizes and modification times alone, a photo in photos by destination the
handoff does not record at its path, one the handoff records in photos by date or by destination that is gone, or one
it records in photos by destination whose size or `mtime_ns` differs from its record: `geotag plan` stops on it with
the one re-prep blocker, and runs prep itself when {need}`BLD-geotag_auto_reprep` allows; prep's nothing-to-do guard
does not stop while it names one.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-reprep_pending.title: What prep has yet to record

BLD-rerun_recognition.content:
Geotag SHALL record what it wrote in the file's `GPSProcessingMethod`: the bare value `interpolated`, `manual_locked` or
`manual_fallback` beside each position it writes, and, when it fixes the time and writes no position, the suffix
`+carto-time` appended once to whatever the field held, keeping the device's own value. Any other value is the device's
own, and the GPS beside it native.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-rerun_recognition.title: Geotag marks what it wrote

BLD-rerun_writes_only_differences.content:
A write SHALL be planned only where the file does not already hold its value, names being recomputed from the
destination's local time, a file already so named getting no rename (geotag §27, §28.2).
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-rerun_writes_only_differences.title: A re-run plans only the writes and renames that differ

BLD-resolved_utc.content:
`compute_resolved_utc` SHALL resolve each photo of photos by destination to UTC: a camera's photo by the offset of its
cell — `<group>@<date>` where the destination has one for its date, else `<group>` — a corrected offset from
`photos-22-gps-drift-validation.json` taking its place (`camera_group_offset`); a phone's by the offset recorded with
its time's field — `OffsetTimeOriginal` for `DateTimeOriginal`, `OffsetTimeDigitized` for `CreateDate`, `OffsetTime`
for `ModifyDate` (`smartphone_native_offset`) — else its destination's timezone (`destination_timezone`); and a time
geotag already corrected by its own offset, else the timezone (`geotag_corrected`); every other photo `unresolved`.
`geotag plan` writes the rows — `relative_path`, `destination_path`, `destination_timezone`, `camera_group`,
`time_decision_scope` (the cell, `<group>[@<date>]|<destination>`), `source_naive_time`, `source_time_provenance`,
`time_rule_used`, `utc_offset_used`, `resolved_utc`, `resolved_utc_status`, `resolved_utc_provenance` — into the
`resolved_utc_cache` table once photos-22 is complete, replacing the table whole.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-resolved_utc.title: How each photo's true time is resolved

BLD-resolved_utc_fingerprint.content:
`resolved_utc_cache_fingerprint` SHALL be the SHA-256 over the rows ordered by path — each its `relative_path`,
`resolved_utc`, `resolved_utc_status`, `time_rule_used`, `utc_offset_used` and `source_time_provenance` as text — and
the inputs, sorted by name: `camera_time_policy_fingerprint`, `camera_group_key_version`, the SHA-256 of photos-21 and
of photos-22, `prep_cache_fingerprint`, `metadata_field_set_version` and `gpx_fingerprint`, the last whether or not a
track decided anything.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-resolved_utc_fingerprint.title: The resolved-UTC fingerprint

BLD-seal_marker.content:
The seal SHALL be `photos-00-sealed.json` in the control directory, its own file beside the workspace guard — which only
prep writes — recording `sealed`, the merge run id (`merged_run_id`) and `library_root`; its presence alone seals.
BLD-seal_marker.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-seal_marker.title: The seal

BLD-seed_before_fingerprints.content:
Prep SHALL seed the configuration at the start of its run, before any fingerprint of it is taken, so that every
fingerprint, the handoff's recorded hash among them, is of the file as it stands in the workspace.
BLD-seed_before_fingerprints.section_name: 3. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
sections: 3. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-seed_before_fingerprints.title: The configuration is seeded before it is fingerprinted
