BLD-shape_guards_by_phase.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-shape_guards_by_phase.title: Where each phase applies the shape guards

BLD-sidecar_extensions.content:
The editing sidecars SHALL be the files ending `.xmp`, `.dop` or `.pp3`, matched ignoring case — a fixed list, not
configuration.
BLD-sidecar_extensions.section_name: 6. What prep refuses to work on
sections: 6. What prep refuses to work on
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-sidecar_extensions.title: The sidecars prep refuses

BLD-snapshot_is_zfs.content:
The snapshot SHALL be a ZFS snapshot, configured by the `zfs` block of the workspace configuration,
`photos-00-config.json`; with no `zfs` block, or one not enabled, none is taken. Its name carries the plan id.
`snapshots_required` decides what a failed snapshot means: true, the run aborts before its first change; false, or the
block not configured, it proceeds without one.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-snapshot_is_zfs.title: The snapshot is a ZFS snapshot, configured by the `zfs` block

BLD-staleness_by_field_fingerprints.content:
Staleness SHALL follow the dependencies each record carries ({need}`DEF-dependency_cascade`): a plan depends on the
whole configuration's hash, a costly result on the hash of the areas it reads.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-staleness_by_field_fingerprints.title: Staleness follows the field-scoped fingerprints

BLD-stray_media_probe.content:
Prep's plan SHALL ask exiftool the `MIMEType` of one file for each distinct extension among the inbox's files of no
media class, and warn for each whose type is `image/*` or `video/*`; with exiftool absent, it warns of none.
BLD-stray_media_probe.section_name: 6. What prep refuses to work on
sections: 6. What prep refuses to work on
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-stray_media_probe.title: One probe per stray extension

BLD-strays_per_run.content:
Prep SHALL move a run's strays into `1-strays/<plan-id>/`, each at its path under `0-sources/`, so that no two runs
share a folder there.
BLD-strays_per_run.section_name: 3. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
sections: 3. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-strays_per_run.title: A run's strays go to `1-strays/<plan-id>/`

BLD-summary_counts_reuse.content:
Each phase's report SHALL count the files already right, and the work it took from a cache: prep's summary its cache
hits, merge's plan the library fingerprints it reused — in what it prints, never in the plan, which an unchanged
re-plan leaves byte-identical. Geotag keeps no cache of results, so has none to count.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-summary_counts_reuse.title: A run's summary counts what it reused

BLD-temp_sweep.content:
Merge's `execute` SHALL, after revalidating its plan and taking its snapshot and before its first move, remove every
`.tmp-xdev-*.part` file directly in `library_root` and in each planned target's directory, and record how many in
`photos-31-merge-summary.json` as `run_metadata.orphan_temps_swept`.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-temp_sweep.title: Merge's sweep of temporary copies

BLD-timezone_cell.content:
Each destination's `destination_timezone` in `photos-21-time-decisions.json` SHALL hold `proposed_iana_timezone` with
its `proposal_source` — `inherited`, naming the ancestor in `inherited_from`, or `config_default`, or `none` —
`user_decision.manual_iana_timezone`, `effective_iana_timezone`, `requires_user_input`, `stale_user_decision` and, when
the proposal took effect without the user, `decision_mode: "auto_resolved"`. Destinations are built parent first, so
each takes the `effective_iana_timezone` of its nearest ancestor that has one, `6-photos-by-dest` itself the first,
from `default_folder_timezone`.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-timezone_cell.title: The timezone cell

BLD-timezone_naive_offset.content:
A bucket with no anchor and a destination timezone SHALL be proposed the offset −(the timezone's UTC offset at the
bucket's earliest camera time), daylight saving included, as `proposal_source: "timezone_naive"` with
`proposed_offset_seconds`, `proposed_real_utc` and `proposed_from_timezone`; it takes effect only once accepted.
BLD-timezone_naive_offset.section_name: 19. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
sections: 19. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-timezone_naive_offset.title: The offset derived from the timezone

BLD-tool_workers.content:
Prep SHALL read metadata through persistent `exiftool -stay_open` workers and fingerprint photos through a persistent
`magick -script -` process per thread — each file read, given `-colorspace sRGB -depth 8`, its `%#` printed, then
`-delete 0--1`, a `{ready}` line closing its reply — falling back to `identify` per file where `magick` is absent; it
starts `ffmpeg` per video. Each tool gets two attempts per file, a dead worker restarted between them.
BLD-tool_workers.section_name: 17. Concurrency, determinism, and what a run shows
sections: 17. Concurrency, determinism, and what a run shows
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-tool_workers.title: The tools' workers

BLD-top_level_entries.content:
The top level of an initialized workspace SHALL hold exactly the managed folders `0-sources`…`6-photos-by-dest` and
`.photos-ingest/`, `.photos-ingest-quarantine/`, `.git` and other dotfiles and dot-directories, the inbox being
`0-sources/`. Prep applies the guard (prep §3.1), geotag at startup (geotag §13), merge as its precondition 0a (merge
§3).
BLD-top_level_entries.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-top_level_entries.title: The workspace's top level

BLD-track_file.content:
A track file SHALL be a file named `*.gpx`, `*.kml`, `*.kmz`, `*.fit`, `*.tcx`, `*.nmea` or `*.igc`, in any case. Of
these geotag reads only the `*.gpx` files beneath `gpx_root`.
BLD-track_file.section_name: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
sections: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-track_file.title: A track file

BLD-track_file_blocker.content:
Prep SHALL raise one blocker for each track file it inventories, naming it, and leave it out of the plan (prep §3,
§6.1); execute raises the same blocker for one that appeared after planning ({need}`RUL-new_file_restales_plan`).
BLD-track_file_blocker.section_name: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
sections: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-track_file_blocker.title: Prep's blocker for a track file

BLD-track_points.content:
Geotag SHALL read every `<trkpt>` of each `*.gpx` file under `gpx_root`, its `<time>` as an `xsd:dateTime` — fractional
seconds optional, the zone `Z` or a numeric offset — normalised to UTC; a point lacking `lat` or `lon`, with one out of
range or not a number, lacking a `<time>`, or with a time unparseable or naive is skipped with a warning naming the
file and the point's index, as is a file that cannot be read or parsed. `geotag plan` prints the count of warnings and
the first `GPX_WARNINGS_SHOWN`, with the number of the rest.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-track_points.title: How track points are read

BLD-two_step_case_rename.content:
A filed media file's extension SHALL be lowercased by two no-clobber renames in its folder, through a temporary name
free on disk and in the plan; an inbox file's, in the move that files it.
sections: Prep — how this build does it
BLD-two_step_case_rename.title: A filed file's extension is lowercased in two renames

BLD-unidentified_files.content:
A file whose `camera_group_key` is `NO_IDENTITY_KEY` (`unknown`), the key prep gives a file with no serial, make, model
or owner, SHALL be classed `unidentified` by `recognize_camera_groups` whatever the configuration lists, never among the
unknown groups, given no offset cell, and resolved as a phone's photo is, its own offset's rule being
`unidentified_native_offset`.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-unidentified_files.title: Files naming no camera

BLD-unknown_group_snippet.content:
On an unknown camera group, `geotag plan` SHALL print the `device_groups` arrays `fixed_clock_cameras` and `phones`,
in the configuration's own key order, each the configured list with every unknown key appended, as JSON to paste over
the configuration's, and exit with status 2 having written no record and read no track.
sections: Geotag — how this build does it
BLD-unknown_group_snippet.title: The classification snippet

BLD-untimed_mark.content: The untimed name SHALL be `UNKN_<name it came with>`, with the `-NNN` suffix when that is taken.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-untimed_mark.title: The `UNKN_` mark

BLD-whole_hash_in_the_plan.content:
The whole-file fingerprint SHALL be carried in the `depends_on` of geotag's executable plan (geotag §28, in the
flattened dependency set of geotag §5) and of merge's plan, `config_fingerprint`, each plan refused when it no longer
matches the file.
BLD-whole_hash_in_the_plan.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-whole_hash_in_the_plan.title: The whole-file hash is in the executable plan's dependencies

BLD-workspace_database.content:
The workspace database SHALL be SQLite, `photos-00-ingest.db` in `.photos-ingest/`, written by: prep, of the file and
metadata caches (`file_cache`, `metadata_cache`) and their version row (`meta`), through its single-writer path (execute's main
thread); geotag, of the resolved-UTC cache (`resolved_utc_cache`), the values each photo held before geotag first wrote
to it (`original_values`, geotag §24.2); merge, of the library-file fingerprint cache (`library_fingerprint_cache`,
keyed by the library file's absolute path with its size and modification time). Where each photo landed is in merge's
JSON records, not the database. The other databases are scratch, re-derivable and deletable at any time: prep's
plan memo, `photos-00-plan-memo.db` ({need}`BLD-plan_memo`), and geotag's track memo, `photos-00-track-memo.db`.
BLD-workspace_database.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
Shared — how this build does it
BLD-workspace_database.title: The database: its file and its writers

BLD-workspace_guard.content:
The mark SHALL be the file `photos-00-workspace-guard` in `.photos-ingest/`, which the initializing run's execute writes
after every other operation has succeeded; the managed folders it creates are `0-sources` … `6-photos-by-dest`.
BLD-workspace_guard.section_name: 3. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
sections: 3. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
Prep — how this build does it
BLD-workspace_guard.title: The mark is `photos-00-workspace-guard`, written last

BLD-workspace_one_filesystem.content:
`workspace_volume_breaks` SHALL walk every folder of the workspace without following links, comparing each one's device
with the workspace root's and not descending into a folder found on another; prep's and geotag's `run`, and merge's
plan, dry run, execution and in-workspace `init-library`, call it through `workspace_volume_error` as soon as they hold
the workspace lock and, on a folder found elsewhere, report it and exit 2.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-workspace_one_filesystem.title: Each run checks the workspace's devices

CHC-ask_only_what_data_cannot_settle.content: Resolve everything derivable automatically; ask only real judgment questions, and make each one cheap to answer.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
CHC-ask_only_what_data_cannot_settle.title: Ask only what the data can't settle

CHC-local_folder_library.content:
The destination is a plain directory tree on disk (feeds digiKam or Immich), not a cloud service or proprietary
catalog.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
CHC-local_folder_library.title: A local, owned, folder-based library

CHC-photos_matter.content: Because they matter, no original may be lost or silently altered — correctness beats convenience.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
CHC-photos_matter.title: Photos matter; they are irreplaceable, so they deserve care

CHC-total_placement.content:
Every photo ends up on the map — precise where tracks allow, rough or manual where they don't — so the result is a
*map-complete* library, not just the frames that came with a location.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
CHC-total_placement.title: 100% placement, even under GPS scarcity

DEF-archival_package.content:
The **archival package** is one archive, kept with the control records, holding the complete record of a dump's journey
through the pipeline — what was done to its photos and why. It is what the user keeps when the workspace goes away.
DEF-archival_package.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
DEF-archival_package.title: The archival package

DEF-authored_value.content: An **authored value** is one the user writes by hand: a setting of the configuration, or a decision.
DEF-authored_value.section_name: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
sections: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
DEF-authored_value.title: An authored value

DEF-camera_group.content:
A **camera group** is the photos one camera or device took, identified by a key derived from the device-identity
metadata the files carry.
DEF-camera_group.title: A camera group

DEF-config_areas.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
DEF-config_areas.title: What the configuration sets

DEF-configuration.content:
A workspace's **configuration** is the one record of the settings its runs read. It is kept in the workspace, beside
what is processed under it, and it is an input the user authors.
DEF-configuration.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
DEF-configuration.title: The configuration

DEF-container_destination.content:
A **container destination** is a folder in photos by destination that holds destinations but no photo of its own —
photos by destination itself among them, when it holds no photo directly.
DEF-container_destination.title: A container destination

DEF-control_records.content:
A workspace's **control records** are everything cartographer keeps in it besides the media: the configuration, the
plans and the decisions, the journals, the end-of-phase records and the databases. The quarantine's manifests are not
control records: each belongs to the quarantine folder whose duplicates it describes.
DEF-control_records.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
DEF-control_records.title: The control records

DEF-database_image.content:
A phase's **database image** is a copy of the workspace database as it stood at the end of that phase's latest
successful run.
DEF-database_image.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
DEF-database_image.title: A phase's database image

DEF-decision.content:
A **decision** is a value the user records in one of geotag's records for the tool to act on — a destination's
timezone, an accepted time anchor, a clock offset, a confirmed drift check, a manual position, a folder fallback. The
tool *proposes*; the user *decides*.
DEF-decision.section_name: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
sections: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
DEF-decision.title: A decision

DEF-dependency_cascade.content:
The **dependency cascade** is how the phases keep a record from being used once what it was made from has changed: each
record carries what it depends on — media by their fingerprints, other records by their hashes, and settings by a hash
of the configuration or of the areas the record reads — and each use checks them first. Its full name, the
*dependency-fingerprint/hash cascade*, says that it tracks both kinds of identity.
DEF-dependency_cascade.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
DEF-dependency_cascade.title: The dependency cascade

DEF-destination.content:
A **destination** is the folder in photos by destination that directly holds a photo; a folder nested in it that holds
photos is a destination of its own.
DEF-destination.title: A destination

DEF-development.content:
**Development** is the later processing of photos into distribution copies — the JPEG and TIFF breakout — kept in
subfolders of a destination.
DEF-development.title: Development

DEF-finalize.content:
**Finalize** is geotag's closing command, given once the user judges the workspace's media done: it assembles the
workspace's permanent record and its complete transformation log.
DEF-finalize.title: Finalize

DEF-fingerprint.content:
A media file's **fingerprint** is the identity of its content apart from its metadata — a photo's decoded pixels, a
video's streams. Unqualified, *fingerprint* means this.
DEF-fingerprint.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
DEF-fingerprint.title: A fingerprint

DEF-geotag.content:
**Geotag**, the second phase, resolves each photo to its true time, inferring and correcting each camera's clock
offset; places the photos that carry no position along the recorded tracks; and renames each by its corrected local
time.
DEF-geotag.title: Geotag

DEF-hash.content:
A record's **hash** is a digest of its exact bytes — of a numbered record, or of the configuration. Unqualified, *hash*
means this.
DEF-hash.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
DEF-hash.title: A hash

DEF-library.content:
The **library** is the permanent, curated collection the media ends in — outside every workspace, and written only by
merge.
DEF-library.title: The library

DEF-managed_folders.title: The managed folders

DEF-merge.content:
**Merge**, the third phase, runs after a workspace has been geotagged and finalized, and moves its finished photos,
sorted by destination, into the library.
DEF-merge.title: Merge

DEF-operator_loop.content:
The **operator loop** is how the user drives the three phases through one workspace's life: prep organizes a dump; the
user sorts photos into photos by destination; prep records the sort; geotag is re-run, the user deciding what it asks,
until its plan is ready, and executes it; more dumps may follow, each from prep again; finalize closes the workspace's
record; merge moves it into the library. Each phase's own loop is in its own spec; this is the sequence across them.
DEF-operator_loop.title: The operator loop

DEF-plan_memo.content:
The **plan memo** is the scratch database where prep's planning keeps what it read of each media file — its fingerprint
and metadata — with the path, size and modification time it read them at.
DEF-plan_memo.section_name: 10. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
sections: 10. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
DEF-plan_memo.title: The plan memo

DEF-prep.content:
**Prep**, the first phase, takes an unorganized dump and makes it a clean working set: it consolidates the dump,
normalizes extensions, sets duplicates aside (recoverably, never deleting), organizes the media by date, and hands
geotag what it found.
DEF-prep.title: Prep

DEF-recorded_time.content:
A file's **recorded time** is the time of its making that its own metadata holds, as the camera's clock read it:
uncorrected, with no timezone.
DEF-recorded_time.title: A recorded time

DEF-sealed_workspace.content: A workspace is **sealed** once merge has succeeded in it: marked as finished, by a mark only merge writes.
DEF-sealed_workspace.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
DEF-sealed_workspace.title: A sealed workspace

DEF-strays_folder.content:
The **strays folder** is a media-tree folder at the workspace's top level. It holds the files that are not media which
prep moved out of the inbox, one subfolder for each run, their structure kept. It is neither a control record nor any
phase's output.
DEF-strays_folder.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
DEF-strays_folder.title: The strays folder

DEF-timestamp_name.content:
A file's **timestamp name** is the name prep and geotag give it from its timestamp, in the one format the configuration
sets, followed by a differentiating suffix when that name is taken.
DEF-timestamp_name.title: A timestamp name

DEF-tracks.content:
A workspace's **tracks** are the recorded position logs geotag reads as evidence: to propose time anchors, and to place
photos along them by interpolation or extrapolation. The configuration says where they are.
DEF-tracks.section_name: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
sections: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
DEF-tracks.title: The tracks

DEF-transformation_log.content:
The **transformation log** is the human-readable account, photo by photo and keyed by each photo's fingerprint, of
everything done to it and why. Each phase keeps its own, carrying the previous phase's forward.
DEF-transformation_log.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
DEF-transformation_log.title: The transformation log

DEF-untimed_name.content:
A file's **untimed name** is the name prep gives a media file with no recorded time: the name it came with, behind a
mark that says so.
DEF-untimed_name.title: An untimed name

DEF-workspace.content:
A **workspace** is the transient place one ingest happens in: a dump of media enters it, the phases work on it in
turn, and merge moves its finished photos into the library. A run's workspace is the folder it is started in.
DEF-workspace.title: The workspace

DEF-workspace_database.content:
The **workspace database** is the one database of record: what cartographer knows about the workspace's media — each
file's identity and metadata, what each phase derived from them, the values a photo held before geotag first changed
it, and the fingerprints of library files merge has read.
DEF-workspace_database.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
DEF-workspace_database.title: The workspace database

FCT-clocks_drift.content:
Each body's clock is wrong by its own amount, and that amount changes between days (drift, manual resets to local time
in the morning, missed DST). There is no single global offset to find.

*Where one has met it:* The import that landed an hour early; the shots an hour off after a border; a day's frames
scattered because the clock was never set — blamed on negligence or forgetfulness, not on a category.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
FCT-clocks_drift.title: Camera clocks drift — independently, and from day to day

FCT-large_batches.content:
A trip dump or a years-deep library is big and mixed: many RAW/JPEG frames across multiple cameras and phones.

*Where one has met it:* The card one keeps meaning to deal with; the decade of folders; or *"I'll geotag these
someday."*
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
FCT-large_batches.title: A photo batch is large — thousands of frames, several cameras

FCT-partial_track_coverage.content:
The logger's tracks reach *some* of the library, never all of it — so the track alone can never place every frame; the
rest needs fallbacks.

*Where one has met it:* The half-tagged library; the map view with holes where phone-sync missed; the frames that came
with a pin and the many that didn't.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
FCT-partial_track_coverage.title: GPX coverage is partial

INV-authored_values_checked.content:
Every authored value SHALL be checked to be valid before it is used — besides, not instead of, the dependency cascade's
check that it has not changed.
INV-authored_values_checked.section_name: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
sections: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
INV-authored_values_checked.title: No value the user writes is used unchecked

INV-change_only_what_needs.content:
Every phase SHALL change only what its inputs actually require, as far as the work allows — redoing no settled work to
be safe, and leaving no file in a state other than its inputs require.
INV-change_only_what_needs.title: A run changes only what its inputs require

INV-every_change_from_the_record.content:
Every change a phase makes SHALL follow from a decision the user recorded, or from a fixed rule applied to recorded
inputs — never from a choice the tool makes on its own; an execution acts only on a plan made from those.
INV-every_change_from_the_record.section_name: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
sections: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
INV-every_change_from_the_record.title: Every change follows from the record

INV-no_stale_use.aliases: dep-cascade-reject-stale-1, prep-block-on-stale-dependency-1, merge-execute-revalidate-reject-stale-1, geotag-dep-cascade-1, geotag-no-stale-execution-1, geotag-file-exists-not-executable-1, geotag-stale-no-json-1, geotag-no-preserve-stale-auto-gps-1
INV-no_stale_use.content:
No phase SHALL use a record once anything it was derived from has changed: each phase validates what it derives from,
then creates the record, records those dependencies in it, and refuses its use downstream when any of them has changed.
INV-no_stale_use.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
INV-no_stale_use.title: No record is used once what it came from has changed

INV-one_run_at_a_time.content:
At most one cartographer run SHALL act on a workspace at any time — whatever the commands: two runs of one phase, runs
of two phases, a merge, a finalize, or a quarantine prune.
INV-one_run_at_a_time.title: One run at a time

INV-undisturbed_shape.content:
No phase SHALL process an initialized workspace whose shape was disturbed from outside cartographer — an entry at its
top level that does not belong there, a symbolic link among its files, a managed folder missing — without stopping.
INV-undisturbed_shape.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
INV-undisturbed_shape.title: A disturbed workspace is never processed silently

RAT-a_link_escapes_the_tree.content:
Following a symbolic link would let a planned read or write reach a target **outside** the managed tree — a pipeline
escape that breaks the no-clobber and "originals never lost" guarantees and the closed-world assumption the content
fingerprint and de-duplication rest on.
RAT-a_link_escapes_the_tree.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-a_link_escapes_the_tree.title: A followed link escapes the managed tree

RAT-anchor_agreement.content:
A camera's clock is wrong by the same amount all day, so every photo it took with a position agrees on the offset —
and the offset is what they agree on. One photo's closest match can be a coincidence: the same walk on the day before,
a hotel passed morning and evening. Counting every pass by each photo's place, the true offset is the one every photo
supports, a coincidence the one only some do. An average of disagreeing offsets is supported by no photo at all. When
nothing tells two offsets apart, the photos do not say which is right, and the user must.
RAT-anchor_agreement.section_name: 19. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
sections: 19. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
RAT-anchor_agreement.title: Agreement is the evidence

RAT-anchor_evidence_trusted_as_configure.content:
An offset measured from the camera's own positions against the tracks is evidence, not a guess: several frames agreeing
on it is hard to get by accident; one frame could be a coincidence of a slow walk. How much of that to accept without a
look is the user's choice, made once in the configuration rather than asked for every camera on every day. Anchors that
disagree mean something is off — a clock reset in the day, a wrong track — and no setting should paper over that.
RAT-anchor_evidence_trusted_as_configure.title: The camera's own GPS is evidence; the user decides how much

RAT-assumptions_need_acceptance.content:
An offset derived from the timezone assumes the camera was set to local time that day; a fallback inherited from a
parent folder assumes the photos were taken near the parent's point. Both are often right and sometimes badly wrong,
and nothing in the photos can tell which. Applied silently, a wrong one would place a whole day of photos in the wrong
place or the wrong hour, written into the originals; offered for acceptance, it costs one confirmation.
RAT-assumptions_need_acceptance.title: An assumption is the user's to accept

RAT-bands_never_mix.content:
Photos are sorted into destinations and geotagged; videos are kept by date and not corrected. A file in the other kind's
folder would be handled as what it is not — a video sorted where geotag cannot place it, a photo kept where it is never
corrected. Prep never puts one there, so one found there was moved by hand, and only the user knows where it belongs.
RAT-bands_never_mix.section_name: 6. What prep refuses to work on
sections: 6. What prep refuses to work on
RAT-bands_never_mix.title: Photos and videos go separate ways

RAT-bare_first.content:
Bare-first is what makes an uncorrected file's provisional (prep) and final (geotag) names coincide, so geotag plans no
needless rename; the two phases use the identical rule so they never disagree on a name.
RAT-bare_first.title: The first free name makes the two names coincide

RAT-bootstrap_once.content:
Dropping a dump into a bare folder is the most natural first gesture, so the first run takes it as it comes: it builds
the structure around the dump and moves it into the inbox whole, its folders kept, for a dump's folders often carry
meaning — a trip, a day, a card. Afterwards the workspace has an inbox, and the top level is no place for a dump.
RAT-bootstrap_once.section_name: 3. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
sections: 3. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
RAT-bootstrap_once.title: The first gesture bootstraps the workspace

RAT-by_dest_is_the_users.content:
Photos by destination is the user's own sorting: where each photo sits is a decision made by hand, which only the user
can make or change. Prep records what it finds there — a new sort included — and changes nothing, so a decision is
never undone by a run that cannot know why it was made.
RAT-by_dest_is_the_users.section_name: 2. What prep does, and what it leaves alone
sections: 2. What prep does, and what it leaves alone
RAT-by_dest_is_the_users.title: Photos by destination is the user's sorting

RAT-bytes_are_the_safe_check.content:
A record is small and every byte of it can matter — a decision, an offset, a timezone — so the safe check is its exact
bytes: comparing chosen fields would let through a change to a field nobody chose. The handoff is the exception because
prep rewrites its run identifiers on every run; checked by its bytes, a run that changed nothing would make everything
after it stale.
RAT-bytes_are_the_safe_check.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
RAT-bytes_are_the_safe_check.title: A record's every byte can matter

RAT-camera_groups_generated.content: **Camera groups are generated for the user**, ready to paste — leaving only the judgment, not the derivation.
RAT-camera_groups_generated.section_name: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
sections: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-camera_groups_generated.title: The tedious part of a judgment call should be pre-computed

RAT-camera_record_first.content:
A file can hold one field in several places: EXIF, written by the camera; XMP, where other tools mirror it, or keep it
for a file with no EXIF; maker notes, QuickTime and the rest. Which one counts must be the pipeline's stated choice, not
the extractor's internal preference, which no one documents and a new version may change. The camera's own record comes
first. A shutter time is still a shutter time when XMP holds it, so a time missing or a placeholder in EXIF is sought in
the same field elsewhere before another field is tried.
RAT-camera_record_first.section_name: 12. The metadata prep keeps for geotag
sections: 12. The metadata prep keeps for geotag
RAT-camera_record_first.title: The camera's record first, by the pipeline's choice

RAT-case_says_nothing.content:
One camera writes `JPG`, another `jpg`, and a file copied through another system may come back either way; the format
is the same. Matching by case would make the same photo a stray in one dump and a photo in the next.
RAT-case_says_nothing.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
RAT-case_says_nothing.title: Case says nothing about a format

RAT-chosen_offset_has_evidence.content:
Where the photos support several offsets, the user picks the one for the day they were there. That offset is backed
by the camera's own positions on the tracks as much as the recommended one; checking it against the tracks again
would ask the user to confirm on a map what those photos already show — work added to the one case that already
needed them.
RAT-chosen_offset_has_evidence.section_name: 19. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
sections: 19. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
RAT-chosen_offset_has_evidence.title: The evidence is the same whichever offset the user takes

RAT-class_decides_handling.content:
A file's class decides everything the pipeline does with it: a photo is organized by date and geotagged, a video goes to
its own folder, anything else is set aside as a stray. An extension in two classes would leave that undecided; a class
the configuration invented would have no handling, since the phases are written for the classes they know; and an
extension nobody listed is safest set aside, recoverably, rather than guessed at.
RAT-class_decides_handling.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
RAT-class_decides_handling.title: A file's class decides how it is handled

RAT-class_decides_time_model.content:
A phone's clock is set by its network and its zone recorded or found per photo, so each photo is solved alone; a
camera's clock is set by hand, wrong by its own amount each day, so geotag finds one offset per destination and day.
Treat a camera as a phone and its error is never corrected; a phone as a camera and a correct clock is offset. Nothing
in a file's metadata tells them apart reliably, so geotag asks rather than guesses — and writes the classification
out, so only the judgement is the user's.
RAT-class_decides_time_model.title: The class decides how a photo's time is found

RAT-class_from_the_user.content:
Geotag treats the two classes differently: a phone keeps network time and is solved file by file, while a camera's clock
drifts and needs an offset for each group and destination. Guessing the class from a make or a model would be wrong for
some devices, and wrong without anyone noticing. Only the user knows, so a group the configuration does not class stays
unknown and geotag asks.
RAT-class_from_the_user.title: Only the user knows a group's class

RAT-clock_error_window.content:
A track is matched to a photo by place, and places are revisited: the spot a photo was taken may lie on a track from
years before. Closest by distance, that track would "correct" the camera by years. A camera's clock is wrong by its
zone and its drift — hours, not years — so only track times that close to the camera's own count. The window cannot
be the destination's zone: the camera may have been left on home time, and that is exactly what the offset corrects.
RAT-clock_error_window.section_name: 19. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
sections: 19. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
RAT-clock_error_window.title: The same place on another trip is not evidence

RAT-clustering_details.content:
**The consensus-clustering details** of clock-offset inference — clustering rather than averaging is forced by
robustness, but the spread thresholds, the tie-breaks, and the confidence grades are choices.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-clustering_details.title: The consensus-clustering details

RAT-coarse_trigger_for_the_cheap_plan.content:
The whole-file fingerprint restaling the plan is a catch-all guaranteeing no config-driven change is ever silently
missed, even one in an area without its own field-scoped fingerprint. It is intentional belt-and-braces *alongside* the
field-scoped fingerprints, not a contradiction of surgical staleness: they keep the **expensive** derived caches from
restaling on unrelated edits, while the **cheap-to-rebuild** plan simply re-plans on any config change. What surgical
staleness rules out is collapsing the *surgical* caches onto the whole-file hash; using that hash as an additional
coarse trigger for a cheap artifact is consistent with — indeed protective of — surgical staleness.
RAT-coarse_trigger_for_the_cheap_plan.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
RAT-coarse_trigger_for_the_cheap_plan.title: A coarse trigger for the cheap plan, a precise one for the costly caches

RAT-config_changes_chosen.content:
Prep's seeding happens once, before anything is made under the configuration; the user's own edits are the intended way
to change it; the library setup records only the one answer it was asked for. A phase that rewrote the configuration on
its own would change what governs the workspace with nobody having decided it, and restale every plan with no cause the
user can find.
RAT-config_changes_chosen.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
RAT-config_changes_chosen.title: Every change to the configuration is one someone chose

RAT-config_is_a_file.content:
Making the config a file binds it intrinsically to the workspace and to everything processed in it. Hashed and folded
into the dependency cascade, it closes the gap where an ambient config could change a run without leaving a trace; and
archived, it lets a future reader know not only what was decided but **under what configuration**.
RAT-config_is_a_file.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
RAT-config_is_a_file.title: A configuration in a file is bound to what it governed

RAT-configurable_folder_names.content:
**Defaults that are offered, not imposed.** Folder names (`0-sources … 6-photos-by-dest`) are configurable, not
hardcoded — the seven-stage *structure* is the invariant, the *labels* are the operator's. The rigidity is structural
where it must be and accommodating where it can afford to be.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-configurable_folder_names.title: Defaults that are offered, not imposed

RAT-confirmed_one_offset.content:
Confirming is looking at the photos on the track at the times one offset gives. Another offset puts them elsewhere,
and that has not been looked at: carried over, the confirmation would pass an offset nobody checked, or let a
correction found for the old one override the user's new decision.
RAT-confirmed_one_offset.title: What was seen was one offset

RAT-consolidated_log.content:
A **consolidated, self-describing log in one kept folder** — *traceability arrived at, not chosen* (and it is this
traceability that lets the provenance tag above mean anything).
RAT-consolidated_log.section_name: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
sections: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-consolidated_log.title: A choice made weeks earlier must still explain itself on return

RAT-container_holds_defaults.content:
A folder holding only other destinations has no photo to correct: it exists so a timezone or a fallback position can be
set once and reach every destination beneath it. If it asked for anything, it would add work instead of saving it.
RAT-container_holds_defaults.title: A container is a place to put defaults

RAT-content_changed_held.content:
Writing a time or a position changes a photo's metadata and nothing it shows; its fingerprint, taken over the decoded
picture, holds through it — which is why every phase can follow a photo by it. A write after which the picture
differs is something wrong — a tool, a format — that the user must see, not something to record as done; and the
photo's identity is at stake, so only the user can take the new content for it.
RAT-content_changed_held.title: Metadata never moves a pixel

RAT-control_records_found_first.content:
Every phase, the editor and the console must find the control records before reading any of them — and the
configuration, which might otherwise name the place, is itself one of them. A fixed place is also what lets prep leave
it out wholesale, and lets anyone opening an old workspace find its record.
RAT-control_records_found_first.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
RAT-control_records_found_first.title: The control records are found before anything is read

RAT-coordinate_carries_its_method.content:
Completeness means precision now *varies* across the library — so each placement must declare how trustworthy it is
(via the **traceability** the multi-session reality forces — see below).

**Every coordinate carries its derivation method** — native / GPX direct-match / interpolated / extrapolated / manual
— so a rough pin is never mistaken for a precise one.

*Why it is kept:* "I still want to be able to know, at a later date, how that GPS position was assigned - maybe I want
to refine it by image/place recognition for example." A new track needs no tag: it changes the GPX folder, which makes
the GPS decisions stale, and they are regenerated.

*The traceability:* "every decision must be traced, and by incorporating the precision, I allow it even in the final
library."
RAT-coordinate_carries_its_method.section_name: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
sections: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-coordinate_carries_its_method.title: Completeness means precision now *varies* across the library

RAT-costly_step_shown.content:
Fingerprinting again is the costliest thing a plan does, and the reasons for it — a new tool version, a move prep could
not match, a file touched — are invisible until counted. Counting them by reason shows the user why a plan took hours,
and that an unexpected cause is one.
RAT-costly_step_shown.section_name: 17. Concurrency, determinism, and what a run shows
sections: 17. Concurrency, determinism, and what a run shows
RAT-costly_step_shown.title: The costly step is shown

RAT-crash_never_locks_for_good.content:
Runs can die — a power cut, a killed terminal, the system running out of memory — and a dead run cannot release its
lock. Held for good, it would leave the user to find and delete a control file by hand, the one edit the tool otherwise
never asks of them; recognised as stale, it lets the next run go on.
RAT-crash_never_locks_for_good.title: A crash never locks a workspace for good

RAT-crash_not_a_verdict.content:
A long-lived tool process can die for reasons that have nothing to do with the file it was reading. Restarted and tried
again, the file is judged on its own; still failing, it is recorded as failed and blocks or waits, never passed off as
read.
RAT-crash_not_a_verdict.section_name: 17. Concurrency, determinism, and what a run shows
sections: 17. Concurrency, determinism, and what a run shows
RAT-crash_not_a_verdict.title: A crash is not a verdict

RAT-database_is_record.content:
The database is not only a cache that makes re-runs cheap: it holds what nothing else does — the values a photo held
before geotag first changed it, which let any change be undone, and each photo's identity across its moves. Discarded
with the workspace, that knowledge would be lost; kept in two places, the two could disagree. The library keeps no
database because it is the user's own collection, organised as they choose, and merge only adds to it.
RAT-database_is_record.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-database_is_record.title: The database holds what the record cannot rebuild

RAT-database_shows_only_now.content:
The live database is one file that every phase changes, so at any moment it shows only the latest state: what prep
knew is overwritten by what geotag learned. An image taken at each phase's end keeps the database's state at every
boundary, to be opened later and compared.
RAT-database_shows_only_now.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-database_shows_only_now.title: A database shows only now

RAT-database_trusted_next.content:
The next run reuses the database's fingerprints and metadata for every file whose size and time are unchanged. A row
left stale or pointing at a file that is gone would be reused for what it no longer describes; refreshing and pruning at
each execution keeps reuse safe.
RAT-database_trusted_next.title: The database is what the next run trusts

RAT-day_folder.content:
The user sorts photos by date into destinations, and a day is the unit they think in: a day's folder holds what was
shot that day and nothing else. A file's day comes from its recorded time, so a file whose time changed — corrected by
the user — belongs to another day, and one whose time is gone belongs to no day at all.
RAT-day_folder.title: A day of photos is one folder

RAT-day_offset_is_the_cameras.content:
A clock offset belongs to the camera on that day; every photo it took that day shares it, however many arrive later.
Once the photos that gave it are corrected, they no longer anchor anything — dropping the offset then would ask again a
question already settled, or leave the later photos an offset nobody checked.
RAT-day_offset_is_the_cameras.title: The offset is the camera's that day, not the photos'

RAT-decision_withdrawable.content:
An **original-values ledger** keeps what each photo held before the tool first changed it, and every plan decides from
it, so deleting a decision *restores* the prior state.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-decision_withdrawable.title: A decision must be withdrawable

RAT-decisions_are_the_users.content:
A decision is a fact only the user knows — which timezone a trip was in, which offset a camera had, where a photo with
no position was taken. A phase that overwrote one, even with a better-looking guess, would silently put the tool's guess
in place of the user's knowledge; so the tool proposes in fields of its own and never touches the user's.
RAT-decisions_are_the_users.section_name: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
sections: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
RAT-decisions_are_the_users.title: A decision is what only the user knows

RAT-decisions_cascade.content:
Decisions **cascade**: *one far-reaching choice high in the tree is traded for many short-reaching ones* — inherit
unless overridden, remembered across re-runs. (This is where "far-reaching" comes from — a chosen trade, not an
inherent property.)
RAT-decisions_cascade.section_name: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
sections: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-decisions_cascade.title: Asking per-photo would be thousands of short-reaching chores

RAT-decisions_reread_cache_only.content:
Decisions are **idempotently re-read each run**; the fast store is **SQLite as a cache only** — derived, rebuildable,
never the source of truth.
RAT-decisions_reread_cache_only.section_name: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
sections: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-decisions_reread_cache_only.title: Resuming must not mean re-deciding

RAT-decoded_pixel_identity.content: A **decoded-pixel fingerprint** (ImageMagick/ffmpeg), not file bytes, as each photo's stable identity.
RAT-decoded_pixel_identity.section_name: From P1 + F3 — recoverable, and resumable on incremental input
sections: From P1 + F3 — recoverable, and resumable on incremental input
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-decoded_pixel_identity.title: Identity must survive EXIF rewrites and renames

RAT-derivation_version_is_code.content:
The version of the camera-group derivation takes part in the dependency fingerprints, so a change to the derivation is
detectable; it versions the code that computes the key, so only the code can set it.
RAT-derivation_version_is_code.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
RAT-derivation_version_is_code.title: The derivation's version must stay the code's

RAT-destination_is_an_input.content:
A photo's true time and its name come from its destination's timezone and from the clock offset found for its camera
there. A photo is moved to fix a mis-sort; carrying its old destination's answers with it would keep the mistake in
its time and its name, now hidden under the right folder.
RAT-destination_is_an_input.title: The destination is an input to the time

RAT-destination_tree_is_a_hierarchy.content:
The destination tree must be a **hierarchy** — the cascade rides on folder nesting, so a flat or tag-based layout can't
inherit at all, and every value would fall back to per-photo entry.
RAT-destination_tree_is_a_hierarchy.section_name: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
sections: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-destination_tree_is_a_hierarchy.title: Inheritance needs an axis to travel along

RAT-destination_tree_is_the_library.content:
The user builds photos by destination as the library should read — country, city, place — and the library, browsed
folder by folder, is that tree grown over many workspaces. Any transform on the way in, a year prefixed or a level
flattened, would be a decision about the library's organisation the user never made, and one a later workspace could
make differently. Kept the same, a photo's place in the library is the place the user chose for it, and the same on
every run, which is what lets an interrupted merge find its own work.
RAT-destination_tree_is_the_library.title: The destination tree is the library's organisation

RAT-development_after_corrections.content:
Distribution copies made before geotag's time and position corrections would be made from uncorrected photos, and the
corrections would invalidate them. Nor is the workspace a place for processing image files at all: that work belongs
to the library. A development folder's presence alone is the signal; nothing guesses whether it really holds output.
RAT-development_after_corrections.title: Corrections would invalidate development

RAT-discrete_stages.content:
**Discrete, inspectable stages** (the numbered pipeline) — each a real checkpoint; the **filesystem is treated as
truth**.
RAT-discrete_stages.section_name: From P1 + F3 — recoverable, and resumable on incremental input
sections: From P1 + F3 — recoverable, and resumable on incremental input
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-discrete_stages.title: A crash must be recoverable

RAT-drift_invisible.content:
A photo with no position of its own is placed where the track was at its resolved time. With an offset the camera's
GPS measured, that time is evidence; with one assumed from the timezone or written by hand, nothing has checked it.
Wrong by an hour, it slides the whole day's photos an hour along the track — each to a real place on the route, so
none looks wrong — and writes those places into the originals. Seeing a photo against the track at its time is the
check; leaving it unseen must never pass for having seen it.
RAT-drift_invisible.title: A wrong offset moves a whole day along the track

RAT-dry_run_for_looking.content:
A dry run lets the user see what execution would do before it does it. Changing anything would make it a partial
execution, and the user could no longer look without acting.
RAT-dry_run_for_looking.title: A dry run is for looking

RAT-dry_run_reads_the_saved_plan.content:
A simulation is a second path that can disagree with execution: it can pass where execution would fail, or the
reverse. Checking the very plan execution will carry out means what the dry run passed is what runs. A summary is
enough because the whole plan is on disk to read.
RAT-dry_run_reads_the_saved_plan.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-dry_run_reads_the_saved_plan.title: The dry run reads the persisted plan

RAT-dump_folders_kept.content:
A dump's folders are the only trace of where each file came from — a card, a phone, a friend's share — and two files of
one name from different sources sit apart only by them. Lifting the files up into one folder would throw that away and
make the names collide; each file instead leaves the inbox once, straight for where it is filed, under a name made free
in the plan.
RAT-dump_folders_kept.title: A dump's folders say where it came from

RAT-duplicate_found_as_it_was.content:
Quarantine keeps a duplicate to be recovered. Its record must give the path and the name it had when found, or a
restore puts back a file the user never had; and moving or renaming it before setting it aside would be work for
nothing, with a crash between leaving it where no run expects it. Setting duplicates aside before any other stage also
lets the copy kept be chosen from where the copies really are.
RAT-duplicate_found_as_it_was.title: A duplicate's record names where it was

RAT-duplicate_points_at_twin.content:
A file set aside as a copy is recoverable only if one can tell which file it copies. Recorded with the copy kept, the
user can check the pair, and a photo already sorted into a destination is seen to have had its copy set aside.
RAT-duplicate_points_at_twin.section_name: 11. Duplicates and failures beside photos by destination
sections: 11. Duplicates and failures beside photos by destination
RAT-duplicate_points_at_twin.title: A duplicate's record points at its twin

RAT-durable_record.content:
That, in turn, forces the record machinery — and note what is *not* a driver here: auditability and decade-longevity,
are **zero-cost benefits** that fall out of building for resumability.
RAT-durable_record.section_name: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
sections: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-durable_record.title: Durable, resumable record

RAT-each_phase_owns_its_steps.content:
Each phase knows only its own work, so each appends only its own steps; rewriting an earlier phase's would put words in
its mouth. Kept whole through the latest phase, one log tells a photo's full story, and each earlier log stays the true
record of what its phase saw.
RAT-each_phase_owns_its_steps.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-each_phase_owns_its_steps.title: Each phase writes only its own steps

RAT-editor_writes_only_decisions.content: The editor writes **only the `user_decision` field** — never derived or evidence fields.
RAT-editor_writes_only_decisions.section_name: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
sections: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-editor_writes_only_decisions.title: The record must stay an honest statement of *intent*, not a mutable scratchpad

RAT-empty_inbox_end_state.content:
An initialized workspace whose inbox is empty is where every prep run ends. A saved plan there is already carried out:
replaying it would collide with the files it made. Stopping says there is nothing to do. Empty means holding nothing,
as geotag's gate counts it: a folder left in the inbox blocks geotag, which sends the user back to prep, so prep
counting it empty would leave neither phase able to go on; its removal is planned, and execution must carry it out.
RAT-empty_inbox_end_state.title: An empty inbox is the end state

RAT-empty_inbox_means_nothing_waits.content:
An empty inbox is the one sign that nothing is waiting to be organized: geotag and merge refuse to run while it holds
something, and the next dump arrives into a clean place, where nothing left from the last one can be taken for part of
it.
RAT-empty_inbox_means_nothing_waits.title: An empty inbox means nothing is waiting

RAT-every_blocker_at_once.content:
A blocker skipped would let a file be left out with nobody knowing. Reporting every one, not the first found, spares the
user a run for each problem: a dump with three is fixed in one pass.
RAT-every_blocker_at_once.section_name: 6. What prep refuses to work on
sections: 6. What prep refuses to work on
RAT-every_blocker_at_once.title: All the problems at once

RAT-execution_resumable.content:
Execution writes into hundreds of originals one after another, and anything can stop it partway. Run again, it must
know what is done and do only the rest — writing nothing twice, choosing no other name — or a crash would leave a
day half corrected or corrected twice. And what it finds changed since the plan may be its own interrupted write or
the user's edit: only the first is its to finish.
RAT-execution_resumable.title: A crash leaves work, not damage

RAT-extension_entries_must_match.content:
A file's extension is matched lowercase and without its dot, so an entry written otherwise matches nothing, and every
file it was meant for is set aside as a stray without a word. An empty class would do the same to the whole class.
Checking the lists turns that silent loss into a named mistake.
RAT-extension_entries_must_match.section_name: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
sections: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
RAT-extension_entries_must_match.title: A list entry that cannot match sets photos aside unseen

RAT-facts_before_decisions.content:
Geotag decides a clock offset per camera and a timezone per destination; before it does, the user and geotag can see
what each camera group and destination holds — how many files, over what span, how many already placed. Prep reports it
and infers nothing: inference is geotag's, made with evidence prep lacks.
RAT-facts_before_decisions.section_name: 12. The metadata prep keeps for geotag
sections: 12. The metadata prep keeps for geotag
RAT-facts_before_decisions.title: Facts before decisions

RAT-failure_may_be_the_machines.content:
A fingerprint fails as often for the machine as for the file: a tool not installed, a decoder missing, a crash. The user
fixes the machine, not the file, so its size and time do not change; a failure kept would block on after its cause was
gone. Taking it again costs one attempt per run for a file that still fails.
RAT-failure_may_be_the_machines.section_name: 11. Duplicates and failures beside photos by destination
sections: 11. Duplicates and failures beside photos by destination
RAT-failure_may_be_the_machines.title: A failure may be the machine's

RAT-failure_says_nothing.content:
A fingerprint that could not be taken tells nothing of what the file holds: two failures are not two copies, and a
failure is no copy of anything. Outside photos by destination, every file's place depends on knowing whether it is a
copy, so prep stops and names it rather than file it blind. A file in photos by destination is the user's, never set
aside; its failure decides nothing there.
RAT-failure_says_nothing.section_name: 11. Duplicates and failures beside photos by destination
sections: 11. Duplicates and failures beside photos by destination
RAT-failure_says_nothing.title: A failure says nothing of the content

RAT-fallback_nested.content:
A destination inside another lies within it, so the place set for the outer one is a fair guess for the inner one —
and the nearer the ancestor, the fairer. It is only a guess, so it waits for the user's acceptance; once accepted, the
user has chosen to inherit, and a fallback changed above flows down to it, as a timezone does.
RAT-fallback_nested.title: A place inside a place is near it

RAT-fallback_optional.content:
The fallback saves answering, photo by photo, for a folder the tracks miss. A destination whose photos the tracks all
place needs none, and one that does can still be answered photo by photo; to make every destination ask for one would
add the work it exists to save.
RAT-fallback_optional.title: A fallback is a convenience, not a gate

RAT-filed_is_settled.content:
A file outside the inbox was filed by an earlier run or moved there by the user. Moving it again on a later run would
undo either for nothing and churn the names the user and later phases know it by. Only two things move it: a copy of it
found to be better filed, and its own recorded time no longer matching its day.
RAT-filed_is_settled.title: What is filed is settled

RAT-files_say_what_is_done.content:
Prep's plan holds no decision of the user's — it follows from the files, the configuration and the database. After an
interruption the files say what was done; planning again from them finds only what is left, while resuming would trust a
plan made for a workspace that no longer stands. The journal records what happened; it is evidence, not a script.
RAT-files_say_what_is_done.title: The files say what is done

RAT-finalize_apart.content:
Geotag is re-run freely, and assembling the permanent record on each pass would be wasted work. Finalize marks the one
moment the user declares the dump done.
RAT-finalize_apart.title: Finalize stays apart because geotag is re-run

RAT-finalize_only_records.content:
Finalize is the moment the user declares the workspace done, and the package must record what geotag actually left. Were
finalize to change anything, the package would record a state that existed only inside finalize, and finalizing again
could record another; reading only, it can be run again at any time and records the same.
RAT-finalize_only_records.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-finalize_only_records.title: Finalize records what geotag left

RAT-fingerprint_and_hash_opposite_jobs.content:
The two words name a value by the role it plays, not by the algorithm underneath, and the two roles are opposite: one
must be invariant under mutation, the other sensitive to it. They keep different names even though a fingerprint is
itself computed with a hash function.
RAT-fingerprint_and_hash_opposite_jobs.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
RAT-fingerprint_and_hash_opposite_jobs.title: Opposite jobs, so different names

RAT-fingerprint_same_method.content:
Duplicates are found and a photo is followed through every phase by comparing fingerprints, and two fingerprints of one
picture agree only when taken the same way: another ImageMagick may normalize pixels differently, another strategy
hashes something else. A fingerprint whose method is not the one in use, or is unknown, would set two copies of one
photo apart or lose a photo's trail; taking it again costs a decode.
RAT-fingerprint_same_method.title: A fingerprint compares only with one taken the same way

RAT-fix_through_inbox.content:
The user gives a file in missing metadata its time with their own tools, whenever they choose. Moving it back into the
inbox says that they are done; it then goes through prep like any file of a new dump, and no second way into the
pipeline needs keeping in step with the first.
RAT-fix_through_inbox.title: The user's fix goes through the inbox

RAT-folder_changed_like_a_file.content:
Moving files out leaves their folders empty, and the inbox must end empty for the next dump; a day emptied by the sort
should not linger. Removing a folder is a change to the workspace like any other, so it is planned and journaled; and
only an empty one goes, so nothing a folder holds — even what arrived unplanned — is ever lost with it.
RAT-folder_changed_like_a_file.title: A folder is changed like a file

RAT-folder_gps_fallback.content:
A **cascading folder-level GPS fallback** — set one coordinate at a trip's root and it is inherited down the tree (P3
makes this cheap; one answer covers many photos).
RAT-folder_gps_fallback.section_name: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
sections: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-folder_gps_fallback.title: Placement cannot depend on the track alone

RAT-folder_names_are_places.section_name: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
sections: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
RAT-folder_names_are_places.title: A folder's name is a place on disk

RAT-folder_roles_are_logic.content:
The roles — the inbox, the read-only destination tree, the order in which duplicates are retained, which folders are
the photo and video bands — are pipeline logic, so the user sets the names and never the roles.
RAT-folder_roles_are_logic.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
RAT-folder_roles_are_logic.title: A folder's role is pipeline logic

RAT-format_editor_split.content: **Format + editor split**: JSON is the record; the Time/Drift/GPS app is what writes it.
RAT-format_editor_split.section_name: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
sections: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-format_editor_split.title: Intricate, evidence-specific decisions are too error-prone to hand-edit

RAT-format_fixed_per_workspace.content:
Merge never renames a file in the library, so after a change the library holds both formats whatever the workspace
does. Renaming every named file in the workspace would buy consistency for the few weeks a workspace lives, at the cost
of renaming originals in bulk; keeping the format the workspace began with and taking the new one to the next workspace
costs nothing.
RAT-format_fixed_per_workspace.title: One format for a workspace's life

RAT-gates_not_history.content:
What bounds geotag's freedom is a small, fixed set of conditions on the workspace, not a "has geotag run before?" flag.
Each gate names a state geotag cannot work correctly from; none says anything about history.
RAT-gates_not_history.title: Bounded by what is true now, not by a flag

RAT-geotag_reads_the_handoff.content:
Geotag reads no photo: everything it decides from, it takes from the handoff — which files, where, from which camera,
with what times and positions. What the handoff leaves out, geotag cannot know; the strays, which nothing processes, are
left out on purpose.
RAT-geotag_reads_the_handoff.title: Geotag reads the handoff, not the photos

RAT-grouping_computed_once.content:
Two derivations of a camera's identity could disagree: a file grouped one way by prep and another way by geotag would
get another camera's clock offset. And the user classes groups by the key they see, so it must be the same key
everywhere it appears. One derivation, by prep, recorded with the file and reused by geotag, rules out both.
RAT-grouping_computed_once.title: Grouping computed once is never reinvented

RAT-growth_shown.content:
A quarantine that only grows costs space without a word. Reporting its size every run lets the user decide when to
prune, knowing what it holds.
RAT-growth_shown.title: A growing cost is shown

RAT-hand_written_fallible.content:
The user writes the configuration and the decisions by hand, so the tool cannot assume they are well formed. A
mistyped timezone or an unsafe path, reported early as a specific problem in a named place, is fixed at its source;
coerced, half applied or let through, it spoils a later operation, and the change it causes can no longer be
explained. Checking keeps every change explainable and the user its author.
RAT-hand_written_fallible.section_name: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
sections: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
RAT-hand_written_fallible.title: What is typed by hand can be mistyped

RAT-handoff_by_content.content:
Living in the skipped directory is independent of the handoff's role as a dependency: it is invisible to prep's media
scan yet fully verified as a dependency by geotag — verified by content, not by exact bytes, so a run-only refresh of
it does not restale downstream.
RAT-handoff_by_content.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-handoff_by_content.title: The handoff is invisible to the scan, yet verified

RAT-handoff_changes_with_workspace.content:
Geotag's work depends on the handoff and is made stale when it changes. A run that changed nothing must therefore leave
its content as it was; the run's own identity and diagnostics, which differ every time, are kept apart, so that only a
real change — a file filed, sorted or changed — restales geotag.
RAT-handoff_changes_with_workspace.title: The handoff changes when the workspace does

RAT-hash_is_for_change.content: A hash is chosen precisely so it changes on any byte change: detecting change is its whole purpose.
RAT-hash_is_for_change.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
RAT-hash_is_for_change.title: Detecting change is a hash's whole purpose

RAT-idempotent_reruns.content: **Idempotent, diff-based** re-runs; a run over unchanged state is a no-op.
RAT-idempotent_reruns.section_name: From P1 + F3 — recoverable, and resumable on incremental input
sections: From P1 + F3 — recoverable, and resumable on incremental input
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-idempotent_reruns.title: Re-runs must not redo settled work or cause churn

RAT-identical_kept_once.content:
Dumps overlap: the same card copied twice, a phone's backup next to its export. Two copies of one photo would be sorted,
geotagged and merged twice. The fingerprint is over the decoded content, so copies are found whatever their name or
metadata; the media class keeps a RAW and the JPEG from it apart, though they show one picture. The copies beyond the
first go to quarantine, recoverable, and photos by destination is never touched.
RAT-identical_kept_once.title: Identical media is kept once

RAT-identity_survives_edits.content:
A fingerprint is chosen precisely so it stays the same when the pipeline rewrites a photo's metadata or position or
renames the file: a media file's identity must survive those mutations, which is what makes it the identity spine the
transformation log and de-duplication rely on.
RAT-identity_survives_edits.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
RAT-identity_survives_edits.title: A file's identity outlives its edits

RAT-image_replaced_not_kept.content:
Never overwriting guards photos, which cannot be made again. An image can: it is a copy of the live database, and only
the latest end of each phase is worth keeping, so a phase's next successful run replaces its image — whole, so that a
capture interrupted leaves a usable image either way.
RAT-image_replaced_not_kept.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-image_replaced_not_kept.title: An image is regenerable; a photo is not

RAT-invalid_decision_shown.content:
Erasing an invalid decision would take away the very thing the user must see to correct it. Kept and marked, it shows
what was written and what is wrong with it.
RAT-invalid_decision_shown.section_name: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
sections: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
RAT-invalid_decision_shown.title: The user keeps what they wrote

RAT-jobs_buy_time.content:
Applying a plan in parallel only saves time, and how many jobs suit depends on the machine of the day. If the count
could change which name a photo got, or what a record says, the outcome would turn on how a run happened to be timed —
neither reproducible nor what the user reviewed. So every choice is made before the parallel work starts, each worker
touches only its own files, and the results are gathered in a fixed order.
RAT-jobs_buy_time.section_name: 16. Nothing changed outside a validated plan
sections: 16. Nothing changed outside a validated plan
RAT-jobs_buy_time.title: Jobs buy time, not outcomes

RAT-journal_is_evidence.content:
After an interruption, the journal is the only record of what the run did. Rewritten in place, a crash mid-save would
leave it truncated — the evidence lost at the one moment it is needed, and the handoff unable to vouch for it.
RAT-journal_is_evidence.title: The journal is the evidence of an interrupted run

RAT-journal_is_the_account.content:
The journal is the history of a run: what it changed, in what order, and how each change ended. The logs are built from
it and the archival package keeps it, so a change missing from it is a change no record explains — the one thing the
record exists to prevent.
RAT-journal_is_the_account.section_name: 16. Nothing changed outside a validated plan
sections: 16. Nothing changed outside a validated plan
RAT-journal_is_the_account.title: The journal is the run's own account

RAT-keep_further_along.content:
A copy in photos by destination carries the user's sort, and one already filed has been named and placed; keeping the
copy furthest along saves redoing that and never moves what the user arranged. The folders are taken as they are before
the plan moves anything, so a new dump never displaces a file already filed, and the order by path makes the choice the
same on every run.
RAT-keep_further_along.title: The copy kept is the one further along

RAT-library_and_workspace_apart.content:
A library inside the workspace would be merged into itself, the tool walking its own output as input. A workspace
inside the library is no safer: the library's own tools, digiKam among them, watch the library's folders and would take
the workspace's working copies — not yet geotagged, not yet named — for photos of the library, each to appear twice once
merged; and a destination folder named as the workspace would place photos inside it. Kept apart, each is only what it
claims to be.
RAT-library_and_workspace_apart.section_name: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
sections: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
RAT-library_and_workspace_apart.title: The library and the workspace lie apart

RAT-library_is_evidence_of_move.content:
The journal is written after a move, so a crash or a Ctrl-C can leave a photo in the library with no entry for it; and
the library is the user's, so a photo a journal entry vouches for may since have been moved or replaced there. Either
way the journal and the library disagree, and only the library says where the photo is. Trusting the journal would
block forever a photo safely placed, or seal a workspace whose merge log names a library file that no longer holds the
photo — a record the user would rely on to find it. Fingerprinting the place again settles it, and costs a read only on
a resume.
RAT-library_is_evidence_of_move.title: The library is the evidence of a move

RAT-library_is_ground_truth.content:
The library is the user's curated collection: its organisation and names are the ground truth, and other tools and
people rely on them. So merge adds to it and changes nothing in it, and assumes it is in order rather than scanning it:
scanning a whole library to place one batch would cost far more than it saves. Where a name is taken, only the content
tells a copy already present from a different photo sharing a name — and where the content cannot be read, nothing
does: a guess either way is a duplicate placed or a photo lost from the workspace, so the photo waits.
RAT-library_is_ground_truth.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
RAT-library_is_ground_truth.title: The library is the user's, and already in order

RAT-library_mark.content:
The library is the user's: it has no structure of the tool's to inspect, so one mark, made once and on purpose, is
all that tells it from any other folder. Checking the mark before anything is written there — the lock included —
keeps the tool from writing into a folder that was never made a library.
RAT-library_mark.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
RAT-library_mark.title: A library has nothing of the tool's to inspect

RAT-library_reads_cost.content:
Fingerprinting a library file means reading and decoding it whole, and the library may sit across a network. Kept in the workspace, a
fingerprint already taken spares that read on the next run, and stays right while the file is unchanged. A kept
fingerprint is trusted by size and modification time, though, and removing a photo because the library already holds
it cannot be undone: that one decision reads the file again rather than trust what was kept.
RAT-library_reads_cost.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
RAT-library_reads_cost.title: A library file costs a full read

RAT-library_shared.content:
Many workspaces merge into one library, each under its own lock. Only a lock on the library itself keeps two of their
merges from writing it at once.
