RAT-library_shared.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
RAT-library_shared.title: One library, many workspaces

RAT-library_snapshot_alone_loses.content:
Merge's changes land in two places: it adds each photo to the library and removes it from the workspace. Rolled back
alone, a snapshot of the library takes the merged photos out of the library while the workspace no longer holds them —
the rollback loses them, a rollback point that destroys what it should protect. A snapshot of the workspace alone is
safe: rolled back, it gives the photos back to the workspace while the library keeps them, a duplicate the next merge
finds already present. So merge snapshots the workspace always, the library beside it where it can, and never the
library alone; with no snapshot of the workspace it takes none at all, and says this merge has no rollback point.
RAT-library_snapshot_alone_loses.title: A snapshot of the library alone would lose what merge moved

RAT-linux_and_open_source_not_roots.content:
This is built and run on Linux, but Linux is not a root — the design is plain Python shelling out to `exiftool`,
ImageMagick, and `ffmpeg`, all cross-platform, so it would port with little structural change. Open-source is likewise
a downstream expression of the "local, owned" ethos (P1, P2), not a structural driver. Neither forces anything below.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-linux_and_open_source_not_roots.title: Linux and open-source are not roots

RAT-live_lock_never_taken.content:
Taking over a lock whose owner is still running would let two runs change the same originals at once — the very thing
the lock exists to stop. Leaving a stale lock alone costs a retry; taking a live one could cost photos. So a doubtful
owner counts as alive.
RAT-live_lock_never_taken.title: A live lock is never taken

RAT-lock_and_revalidation.content:
This whole-run lock is independent of, and stricter than, the dependency-revalidation discipline: revalidation guards
against *stale* inputs across separate runs, while the lock guarantees runs never overlap in the first place.
RAT-lock_and_revalidation.title: The lock and revalidation guard different things

RAT-log_adds_no_authority.content:
The log is for reading, not deciding: it gathers what prep's own records already say into one account per photo. Made
from them alone, it can be checked against them and never contradicts them; and a set-aside copy appears beside the
photo it copies, so the account of that photo is whole.
RAT-log_adds_no_authority.title: The log adds no authority

RAT-log_read_by_people.content:
The log outlives the tool that wrote it: it is read by a person, years on, perhaps without cartographer at hand. A
stable order lets two logs be compared line by line; names and values as people say them — a time with its timezone, an
offset in hours and minutes — need no program to decode.
RAT-log_read_by_people.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-log_read_by_people.title: The log is read by people, years on

RAT-longevity_is_free.content: *(zero-cost benefit)* Decade-longevity and "open one folder years later" come free — incidental, never the driver.
RAT-longevity_is_free.section_name: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
sections: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-longevity_is_free.title: Built to survive a three-week gap, it survives a thirty-year one

RAT-loop_is_steady_state.content:
The loop is a steady state to return to, not a one-way pipeline: a batch can be imported, sorted, and followed by
another before anything is geotagged. A phase that judged by what ran before would have to forbid that; one that judges
the present state need not.
RAT-loop_is_steady_state.title: A steady state to return to

RAT-mark_in_the_file.content:
What geotag did to a photo is marked in the photo itself rather than kept only in the workspace: the mark survives the
workspace, reaches the library, and is read back wherever the photo turns up again, so a photo corrected once is
recognised as corrected whichever workspace it is in.
RAT-mark_in_the_file.title: The file carries the record of what geotag did

RAT-mark_means_whole.content:
The mark says the workspace is whole. Written before the folders, a run that died halfway would leave a workspace marked
whole but missing a folder, and every later run would refuse it as disturbed; written last, a dead run leaves no mark,
and the next simply initializes again.
RAT-mark_means_whole.section_name: 3. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
sections: 3. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
RAT-mark_means_whole.title: The mark means the workspace is whole

RAT-mark_once.content:
A file comes in already marked when the user sends it back from missing metadata: they gave it a time, or meant to. If
it still has none it returns to missing metadata, and the name it had there is the one the user knows it by; marking it
again would grow its name on every round and say nothing new.
RAT-mark_once.title: A file sent back keeps the name it had

RAT-memo_is_observation.content:
A memo entry says only that a file at a path read so; the database says what prep's executions left. So the database
wins where both speak, an entry is held to the database's tests, and an entry proves no move — a plan never executed
says nothing of where any file went. The memo saves reading and nothing else, so with it, without it, or with it
broken, prep plans the same.
RAT-memo_is_observation.section_name: 10. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
sections: 10. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
RAT-memo_is_observation.title: The memo is an observation, not a record

RAT-merge_appends.content:
In the library a gap in the numbers is a photo the user deleted; giving its number to a new photo would hand it a name
a backup or an export may still use for the deleted one.
RAT-merge_appends.title: The library is append-only

RAT-merge_never_half_done.content:
Finalize is a point in time, and photos by destination can change after it. Merge checks the finalized set against the
present one rather than trusting finalize was last, so a half-geotagged set cannot reach the library.
RAT-merge_never_half_done.title: Never a half-geotagged set in the library

RAT-merge_outcome_decides_next.content:
What the user does after a merge turns on how it ended: nothing after a whole success, a fix and another run after a
partial one or a failed one, and after a refusal a fix with nothing to undo, the library untouched. Counts alone cannot
tell a refusal from a run that found nothing to do; a recorded outcome says which, long after the terminal has gone.
RAT-merge_outcome_decides_next.section_name: 9. User-visible outputs and the merge summary
sections: 9. User-visible outputs and the merge summary
RAT-merge_outcome_decides_next.title: The run's end decides what to do next

RAT-merge_report_at_the_end.content:
Merge is the step that puts photos where the user will look for them, and the one that ends the workspace. Its report
is the moment the user learns whether the batch is in, which photos are not and what to fix — without opening the
summary — and that the workspace is now finished, so the next dump belongs in a fresh one.
RAT-merge_report_at_the_end.section_name: 9. User-visible outputs and the merge summary
sections: 9. User-visible outputs and the merge summary
RAT-merge_report_at_the_end.title: Merge is the step the user watches

RAT-minimal_cascading_asks.content:
Such intricacy would be brutal to enter by hand, so P3 (ask only what the data can't settle) governs how it is
collected — and introduces the document's central trade.
RAT-minimal_cascading_asks.section_name: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
sections: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-minimal_cascading_asks.title: Minimal, cascading asks

RAT-misnamed_not_ignored.content:
Outside the inbox every name is one the pipeline gave. A name that is not means a file was renamed or put there by
hand, and nothing says which time or which photo it holds; passed over in silence, it would reach the library under a
name that looks trusted. Only the inbox takes files as they come.
RAT-misnamed_not_ignored.title: Outside the inbox, every name is the pipeline's

RAT-move_launders_nothing.content:
A move changes where a file is, not what it is, so what prep knows of it still holds — but only as far as it held before
the move. A row that would have been read again where it was is no better for being carried; carrying it unread would
keep under the new path what the old path would have refreshed. Yet it is still the same file: a new ImageMagick or
exiftool is a reason to check what the row says, never to forget whose it is. Forgotten, the user's sort would read as
a new file, and a fingerprint that changed with it would part the photo from its history.
RAT-move_launders_nothing.section_name: 10. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
sections: 10. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
RAT-move_launders_nothing.title: A move launders no stale row

RAT-move_not_copy.content:
A copy left in the workspace of a photo already in the library is a duplicate that invites confusion and wastes space,
so merge moves rather than copies, and removes a copy whose content the library already holds. What stays behind is
exactly what still needs attention. Removing the workspace's copy last, once the library's is verified, means an
interruption never loses a photo: running merge again finishes the work.
RAT-move_not_copy.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
RAT-move_not_copy.title: The workspace keeps only what still needs attention

RAT-multi_session_job.content:
This is a **two-level chain**: a fact and a choice together force an intermediate consequence, and that consequence
forces the record machinery. It is the part most easily mistaken for an arbitrary choice.

Neither root does it alone. Scale (F1) without the 100%-coverage goal (P4) is fast: prep is automated, one keeps the
native-GPS frames, lets the track cover the easy matches, and stops — plausibly one sitting, because the long tail is
never chased. The goal without scale is also trivial: placing ten photos completely takes minutes. Only *total
coverage across a large, mixed batch* produces a long tail of per-(camera, destination, day) offset confirmations and
hand-placed remainder that cannot be finished in one sitting.

Note: not all of that elapsed time is P4's. The album **sort** into a destination tree is owed to **P2** — one would
drag photos into folders even with no geotagging at all — so P2 contributes session-spanning human time on its own.
What F1 + P4 *specifically* add is the **long tail of confirmations and manual placement** that has no automated
escape. Either way, the job likely spans multiple sessions.

**Intermediate consequence — a multi-session job.** The machine cannot hold one's decisions in its head between
sittings.
RAT-multi_session_job.section_name: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
sections: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-multi_session_job.title: A multi-session job

RAT-name_in_local_time.content:
A name is read by a person looking for a photo, who remembers the time of day where it was taken. A camera's clock may
be off or still on home time, and UTC is nobody's time of day; the corrected time at the destination is the one that
matches the memory.
RAT-name_in_local_time.title: A name in the time of day where the photo was taken

RAT-names_cannot_key_the_log.content:
A photo is renamed up to twice in the workspace — a provisional name, then its final one — and may be renamed again on
its way into the library, so no name identifies it across its journey. Its fingerprint does: it survives every rename,
move and metadata write the pipeline makes.
RAT-names_cannot_key_the_log.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-names_cannot_key_the_log.title: A name cannot key the log

RAT-names_never_collide.content:
Photos taken in the same second — a burst, two cameras — get the same timestamp name, and a name given twice would
overwrite an original. The suffix keeps every one; counting the names already planned as taken stops two files of one
run from claiming the same name, and comparing without case keeps them apart on a filesystem that ignores case.
Allocated deterministically, a re-run gives each file the name it gave before.
RAT-names_never_collide.title: Two files never share a name

RAT-nearest_timezone.content:
The destination a place lies in is the most specific word on its timezone: Kyoto inside Japan is in Japan's zone. The
configured default is the user's usual zone, true of no trip in particular, so it fills in only where the tree says
nothing. And a zone the user sets on a trip's folder should hold for everything beneath it — one answer for the trip,
not one per folder.
RAT-nearest_timezone.title: The nearest place says the most

RAT-nested_place_same_timezone.content:
Destinations nest geographically — a city in a country, a museum in a city — so one inside a destination of known
timezone can scarcely lie in another. Asking the user to confirm it for every folder would be asking what the tree
already says. Where the tree says nothing — no ancestor and no default — there is nothing to propose, and the user must
answer.
RAT-nested_place_same_timezone.title: A nested place is in its parent's timezone

RAT-never_behind_prep.content:
Geotag depends on prep's handoff, and a photo prep has not recorded is not in it. Re-prepping after every sort, even
after geotag has run, keeps the handoff the whole truth about photos by destination.
RAT-never_behind_prep.title: New photos never reach geotag behind prep's back

RAT-new_fingerprint_same_photo.content:
The log follows a photo by its fingerprint. When the method that takes it changes — another ImageMagick — the same
pixels can come out under a new value. Left as it was, the old entry would point at a photo the workspace no longer
names, and the photo would start again with no history, marked partial. The file it was left at, now holding the new
value while the old one is nowhere, says it is the same photo.
RAT-new_fingerprint_same_photo.title: A new fingerprint is not a new photo

RAT-new_version_may_change_nothing.content:
A new ImageMagick usually decodes the same pixels to the same fingerprint, but nothing promises it. Trusted blindly, a
fingerprint from the old version compared with one from the new can call one photo two; discarded blindly, a photo
loses whatever is keyed by its fingerprint. Taking it again settles which: most often the value is the same and nothing
moves; where it is not, the photo is still the one it was, and what was recorded of it must follow, or wait.
RAT-new_version_may_change_nothing.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
RAT-new_version_may_change_nothing.title: A new version may change nothing

RAT-no_automatic_deletion.content: Duplicates are **quarantined**, never removed; pruning is an explicit, separate act.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-no_automatic_deletion.title: Deletion is never automatic

RAT-no_borrowed_offsets.content:
Folders nest by geography, which is why a timezone or a fallback position can pass down them; a clock's error does not
follow geography. A museum visited inside a city trip may be another day, the camera reset in between; a parent
folder's offset averaged from its children would be right for none of them. An offset borrowed would look measured
while it is not — so each is proposed from the camera's own positions that day, or from the timezone, and labelled as
such.
RAT-no_borrowed_offsets.title: One place's clock evidence says nothing of another's

RAT-no_chain_of_vouching.content:
The decision records are files the user edits between runs, in the editor or by hand. If the plan named only the last
of them and trusted it to name the rest, a change upstream of it — a track added, an earlier record edited after the
later one was written — would pass unseen whenever the later record happened not to be rewritten. Carried in the plan
itself, every input is checked against what it is now, at the one moment that matters: just before anything changes.
RAT-no_chain_of_vouching.title: A chain is only as fresh as its weakest link

RAT-no_hidden_litter.content: Hidden dotfiles are swept to the recoverable quarantine, not merely skipped, so a dump leaves no hidden litter.
RAT-no_hidden_litter.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-no_hidden_litter.title: A dump leaves no hidden litter

RAT-no_identity_no_group.content:
Screenshots, scans and photos a messaging app stripped name no camera, and share nothing but that. Taken for one camera,
they would be asked to be classed as one and, classed a camera, given one clock offset per destination and day — an
offset no camera of theirs had. Each carries what time it has; read alone, as a phone's photo is, by its own offset or
the place's zone, it asks nothing and borrows nothing.
RAT-no_identity_no_group.title: No camera, no clock to correct

RAT-no_migration.content:
A workspace lives from one dump to its merge, and the database is rebuilt from the files by any fresh workspace. A
migration would be code kept for databases that do not exist, run on the one record that cannot be checked against
anything else; a database of another schema read as this one would be read wrong. Stopping says so, and a fresh
workspace is the remedy.
RAT-no_migration.title: No old workspace to migrate

RAT-no_mutation_outside_plan.content: **plan → validate → execute**; the dry-run *is* the serialized plan; stale plans are rejected against current state.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-no_mutation_outside_plan.title: No mutation outside a validated plan

RAT-no_phase_invents_time.content:
A photo with no recorded time has nothing to correct and nothing to look up: its true time is unknown, and no
camera's offset or destination's timezone can supply one. Prep sets such a photo aside in missing metadata for the
user to deal with by hand. Sorted into a destination anyway, it would pass through geotag's decisions with nothing to
ask about it and stop only at the last plan, where nothing the user could decide would clear it. Stopping at the start,
naming it and where it belongs, makes the one possible fix plain.
RAT-no_phase_invents_time.title: No phase invents a time

RAT-no_redo_to_be_safe.content:
Settled work done again "to be safe" makes nothing safer: a file written with what it already holds gains nothing and
risks a failed write, and reading a library's content again can cost hours.
RAT-no_redo_to_be_safe.title: Redoing settled work buys no safety

RAT-non_destructive_core.content: plan / validate / execute; atomic no-clobber; quarantine, not delete; original-values ledger.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-non_destructive_core.title: Non-destructive core

RAT-offset_per_camera_destination_day.content:
Start with the fact. Because each camera's clock is wrong by its own amount, and that amount changes from day to day
(F2), there is no single offset to discover — the correct answer is **per (camera group, destination, day)**. *That*
granularity is the entire source of the decisions' "complexity": it is a consequence of real, time-varying drift, not a
premise.

The offset is **inferred and applied per (camera group, destination, day)**; corrections fall *between* destinations,
never within one — which is why **one destination = one coherent shoot**.
RAT-offset_per_camera_destination_day.section_name: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
sections: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-offset_per_camera_destination_day.title: Drift is per-camera and per-day, so no global offset is correct

RAT-offset_per_day_and_place.content:
A camera's clock drifts, and is set again — to local time, on a trip, often each morning. Its error is one amount for
one day's shooting and another the next, and destinations are where the user went, not when; one offset per camera, or
per destination over several days, would be wrong for every day but one. A day in one place is the unit within which
the error stays put, so it is the unit decided.
RAT-offset_per_day_and_place.title: A clock is wrong by its own amount, day by day

RAT-one_extension_spelling.content:
Cameras write `.JPG` and `.ARW`; tools and the library match names exactly on many filesystems. One spelling across the
workspace means a name is the same name in every folder and every phase, and two files differing only in an
extension's case are seen as the one name they are.
RAT-one_extension_spelling.title: One spelling of each extension

RAT-one_filesystem_specific_part.content:
The mechanism is named for ZFS because that is the reference implementation, but it is deliberately the *only* part
of the pipeline that touches a specific filesystem feature, and it is optional; everything else is filesystem-agnostic.
RAT-one_filesystem_specific_part.title: Why the snapshot alone may touch the filesystem

RAT-one_format_no_drift.content:
With one format key for the whole pipeline, the provisional names prep assigns and the final names geotag assigns are
guaranteed to share the same textual shape and can never drift apart; there is no format divergence to reconcile.
RAT-one_format_no_drift.title: One key, so the names cannot drift apart

RAT-one_place_for_settings.content:
Settings read from more than one place — a phase's own file, an environment variable, the program's defaults — can
disagree, and a run's result would then depend on where it ran, not on the workspace. With one configuration in the
workspace, everything that governed a run is in one file, hashed, checked and archived with what it governed.
RAT-one_place_for_settings.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
RAT-one_place_for_settings.title: One place for every setting

RAT-one_place_per_plan.content:
A plan kept in one known place is the plan that runs: the dry run and the execution read exactly what the last planning
wrote, and the user always knows where to review it. An option naming another place would let a run carry out a plan
other than the last one made — an old copy, or another workspace's — and would ask the user to remember where they put
it, in a tool used a few times a year.
RAT-one_place_per_plan.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-one_place_per_plan.title: A plan in one known place is the plan that runs

RAT-one_read_serves_both.content:
Prep opens every file anyway, to fingerprint and file it; geotag needs the same files' times, cameras and positions.
Kept by prep, they are read once, and geotag reads no photo. Prep keeps them as recorded and decides nothing from them
({need}`RAT-prep_has_no_evidence`).
RAT-one_read_serves_both.section_name: 12. The metadata prep keeps for geotag
sections: 12. The metadata prep keeps for geotag
RAT-one_read_serves_both.title: One read serves both phases

RAT-one_skipped_place.content:
Skipping the control directory wholesale means a control or artifact file can never be mistaken for a photo. There is
no per-file "ignore list" to maintain — consolidating everything in one skipped directory replaces the basename
registry that earlier designs needed.
RAT-one_skipped_place.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-one_skipped_place.title: One skipped place instead of a list of names

RAT-one_snapshot_mechanism.content: Each phase that mutates uses the same mechanism so the phases behave identically and cannot diverge.
RAT-one_snapshot_mechanism.title: One mechanism, so the phases cannot diverge

RAT-one_source_per_fact.content:
The facts the dependencies are built from — the configuration, the control records, the camera-group derivation's
version, the filename format, the tracks, the snapshot mechanism — are each defined once, for every phase, so that a
single change has one authoritative source and a predictable staleness footprint everywhere.
RAT-one_source_per_fact.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
RAT-one_source_per_fact.title: One source for each shared fact

RAT-one_version_per_comparison.content:
Merge compares prep's fingerprint of a photo with one it takes now of the library file in its way. Taken by two
versions of ImageMagick, two fingerprints of the same pixels may differ: the photo would be called new and placed again,
renamed, beside itself — a duplicate in the library, which merge must never make. Taken again under the version now in
use, prep's fingerprint is confirmed and the comparison holds. A photo whose fingerprint did change waits in photos by
destination: what geotag recorded of it is keyed by the old value, and merging it would carry a record that names no
photo into the library's history.
RAT-one_version_per_comparison.title: One version on both sides of a comparison

RAT-only_sorted_is_ready.content:
A photo's destination is what geotag corrects it by: the timezone of the place, the offset of that camera on that
day, the fallback position of the folder. A photo not yet sorted has none of these, and a file in the other folders is
not a photo to place — a stray, one missing metadata, a JPEG set aside beside its RAW. Videos stay where prep put them:
the pipeline does not place them, and a tag written into one would be a guess. Sorting a photo into a destination is
the user's statement that it is ready.
RAT-only_sorted_is_ready.title: Only what the user sorted is ready

RAT-only_what_geotag_treats.content:
Geotag corrects only photos: it reads and writes photo metadata and places photos on the map. A video or any other file
in photos by destination would reach the library beside photos geotag treated, itself untreated; refusing keeps the
destination's set one geotag has wholly treated.
RAT-only_what_geotag_treats.title: Only what geotag treats goes to the library

RAT-organization_decides_where_files_are.content:
Geotag's and merge's plans locate the destination tree by name and classify the tree, and renaming a managed folder or
moving an extension between media and `other` changes which files exist where. Prep re-plans from the filesystem each
run and guards execution with the whole-file hash, so it needs no separate folder or extension fingerprint of its own.
RAT-organization_decides_where_files_are.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
RAT-organization_decides_where_files_are.title: Folder names and media classes decide which files exist where

RAT-other_outside_inbox_is_the_users.content:
Prep sets files of no media class aside only from the inbox, where a dump arrives mixed. Outside it, such a file got
there another way: an extension the user has since taken off the lists, which turns organized photos into files of no
class, or a file the user put there by hand. Moving it would guess which; leaving it unsaid would keep among the media a
file nothing accounts for. Stopping names it, and the user decides — as for a misnamed file.
RAT-other_outside_inbox_is_the_users.section_name: 6. What prep refuses to work on
sections: 6. What prep refuses to work on
RAT-other_outside_inbox_is_the_users.title: A non-media file outside the inbox got there another way

RAT-own_position_best.content:
A position the camera wrote was measured where the photo was taken. Everything geotag can offer instead is derived —
from a track and a corrected time, from a folder — and so weaker evidence: replacing the measurement with it would make
the photo less right, not more.
RAT-own_position_best.title: The camera measured where it was

RAT-package_answers_later.content:
The workspace is transient; the package is what remains of it beside the library. It must answer later what the
workspace could: under which settings, by which decisions, from which plans each photo was changed, and what each phase
saw. Anything left out — a journal, a snapshot — is a question no one can answer once the workspace is gone.
RAT-package_answers_later.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-package_answers_later.title: The package answers what the workspace could

RAT-package_checks_itself.content:
A package moved to long-term storage is parted from the workspace that made it and may sit untouched for years. Naming
its workspace, plan and execution ties it to what it records; listing every item with its hash lets anyone confirm,
without the tool, that nothing in it has decayed or been altered.
RAT-package_checks_itself.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-package_checks_itself.title: The package can be checked without the tool

RAT-package_records_what_was_done.content:
The archival package is what outlives the workspace: the account of what geotag did to each photo and why. Made
from an execution that did not finish, it would record changes the photos lack; made after a decision was edited
and not executed, it would record a decision they never received. Either way the record would lie about the
library.
RAT-package_records_what_was_done.title: The package records what was done

RAT-partial_merge_no_dead_end.content:
A partial merge leaves the cause of its blockers for the user to fix — a library file that could not be read, a photo
changed — and some fixes change what the plan must say. Until the seal, nothing merge has done is final, and its
records describe what happened rather than gate what may happen next; refusing to re-plan would leave the user with a
plan that can no longer finish and no way to make one that can.
RAT-partial_merge_no_dead_end.title: A partial merge is never a dead end

RAT-phases_rely_on_the_shape.content:
The structural facts are shared by every phase because each relies on them when it scans, and a violation of any one
means the workspace was disturbed out-of-band. The guards compose with — but are distinct from — input validation, which
checks *authored values*, and the dependency cascade, which checks *change*: these check the *shape of the workspace
itself*.
RAT-phases_rely_on_the_shape.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-phases_rely_on_the_shape.title: Every phase relies on the shape when it scans

RAT-phone_records_its_offset.content:
A phone's clock is set by its network and it records the offset it was at, beside each time it writes: better
evidence than any zone geotag could assume. But a photo holds several times, each with its offset — when it was
taken, digitized, modified — and an offset describes only the time it was written with; another would be right only by
chance. Where the photo records none for its time, the destination's zone is the best guess left.
RAT-phone_records_its_offset.title: A phone says its own offset

RAT-photos_wait_by_date.content:
The user sorts photos into destinations from photos by date; ordered by their recorded time, the photos of one trip and
one day sit together, ready to be moved as a block. The timestamp name keeps that order however a folder is listed.
RAT-photos_wait_by_date.title: Photos wait by date for the user's sort

RAT-piggyback_on_the_destination_sort.content:
Timezone, clock offset, and GPS fallback are **piggybacked on the destination sort** one would do anyway for real albums
(P2).
RAT-piggyback_on_the_destination_sort.section_name: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
sections: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-piggyback_on_the_destination_sort.title: The unavoidable human act should pay for itself

RAT-placement_most_specific_first.content:
Each source speaks for fewer photos than the one after it: a position the user set speaks for that photo alone, a track
for the instant it was taken, a fallback for a whole folder. The first that applies is the most specific word on where
the photo was; a photo none of them places is one only the user can answer for — with a place, or by leaving it
unlocated.
RAT-placement_most_specific_first.title: Most specific first

RAT-plain_json_record.content: **Plain JSON** decision artifacts — the durable external record, read back at the start of each session.
RAT-plain_json_record.section_name: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
sections: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-plain_json_record.title: Decisions can't live in the tool between sessions, so they must persist outside it

RAT-plan_before_run.content:
Execution carries out only a plan the user could review first. With none saved, there is nothing reviewed to carry out,
and planning on the spot would skip the review the plan exists for.
RAT-plan_before_run.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-plan_before_run.title: Nothing runs that the user could not review

RAT-plan_can_be_overtaken.content:
A plan is made from the filesystem at one moment, and the workspace or the library can change before it runs. The
plan's own collision check is the first defence; checking each name as it is written is a second, independent one,
which no plan, however careful, can stand in for.
RAT-plan_can_be_overtaken.title: A plan describes the workspace as it was

RAT-plan_is_its_codes.content:
A saved plan is the decisions of the code that made it: names, copies, places, a time and a position for each photo,
a target in the library. Carried out by another build, it would apply decisions the running code would not make — a
fault the upgrade fixed among them, and at merge into the library, the one place nothing is re-planned from. A version
number cannot tell builds apart while every local build carries the same one; the code's own fingerprint can. Planning
again is cheap: prep's memo keeps what it read, merge's cache the library's fingerprints, and geotag plans again from
its decision records.
RAT-plan_is_its_codes.section_name: 16. Nothing changed outside a validated plan
sections: 16. Nothing changed outside a validated plan
RAT-plan_is_its_codes.title: A plan is the decisions of its code

RAT-plan_keeps_its_reading.content:
Decoding photos is most of a plan's cost — hours on a large library — and the user often plans again before executing:
a configuration edited, a folder corrected, a run interrupted. The database speaks only of the executed workspace, so
a plan's reading is kept apart from it, in scratch; kept only for what the latest plan saw, it stays the size of the
workspace.
RAT-plan_keeps_its_reading.section_name: 10. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
sections: 10. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
RAT-plan_keeps_its_reading.title: A plan never executed loses nothing it read

RAT-plan_on_current_record.content:
Geotag decides from what prep read in each photo — its time above all — and never reads the photo again. A photo
removed since would be planned for nothing; one changed since, its time set in another program say, would have that
change overwritten by a time worked out from values it no longer holds — and execution, which must accept a change to
a photo's metadata alone to resume its own writes, cannot tell the two apart. Its size and modification time, against
prep's record, show it without reading it.
RAT-plan_on_current_record.title: A plan on a reading the file no longer holds

RAT-plan_read_before_anything_moves.content:
A plan is there to be read before anything happens — by the user, and by the dry run that checks it. Planning that
changed a file would leave the workspace neither as it was nor as the plan intends, before anyone agreed to either; and
planning again, which the user may do as often as they like, would change it again. So planning only reads, and writes
only what reading produced: the plan, the decisions it asks for, and what spares the next run reading it all again —
and once, the configuration the plan itself is made under.
RAT-plan_read_before_anything_moves.section_name: 16. Nothing changed outside a validated plan
sections: 16. Nothing changed outside a validated plan
RAT-plan_read_before_anything_moves.title: A plan is read before anything moves

RAT-plan_saw_the_workspace.content:
A file that arrived after planning is one the plan never considered: a copy of something it files, or a name it gives
another. Carrying out the plan would leave the file unfiled, or file around it; planning again takes it in, reusing all
that is already known.
RAT-plan_saw_the_workspace.title: The plan is of the workspace it saw

RAT-planning_inside_lock.content:
Planning changes nothing but the fingerprints it keeps for later runs, but it must still not run concurrently: a plan
computed against a workspace another process is reading or changing is untrustworthy, so planning is inside the lock too.
RAT-planning_inside_lock.title: A plan made beside another run cannot be trusted

RAT-position_follows_time.content:
A photo with no position of its own is placed where the track was at the moment it was taken — its true time, after
the camera's clock is corrected. Placed before that time is settled, it would be placed at the wrong moment of the
track, possibly kilometres off, and every position would have to be planned again once the time changed. So the time
is settled for every photo first, and only then is any position planned.
RAT-position_follows_time.title: A position is looked up by time

RAT-position_whole.content:
EXIF stores a latitude and a longitude without their signs: the hemisphere is in a field of its own. A coordinate
written without it is read as no location at all, or put north and east of where it was — a photo from Sydney placed
in the Pacific off Japan. Left behind when the coordinate is cleared, the reference is half a position that some
reader will complete. Whole or not at all is the only safe write.
RAT-position_whole.title: Half a position is a wrong one

RAT-prep_cannot_know_the_time.content:
Prep runs before anyone knows a photo's true time: the camera's clock offset comes from geotag, by matching against the
tracks or from the user, and the timezone from the destination the user sorts the photo into. All prep has is the time
the camera recorded — enough to put a day's photos in order, not enough for a name to keep.
RAT-prep_cannot_know_the_time.title: Prep cannot know a photo's true time

RAT-prep_gatekeeps_links.content:
The destination tree is read-only for prep yet still scanned by it, so prep is also the gatekeeper for links that
appear there; and the mandatory re-prep after any change to it means geotag and merge only ever consume a handoff prep
built with no forbidden link present.
RAT-prep_gatekeeps_links.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-prep_gatekeeps_links.title: Prep is the gatekeeper for links under the destination tree

RAT-prep_has_no_evidence.content:
A photo's true time and place need what prep does not have: the camera's clock offset, found by geotag against the
tracks or given by the user, and the timezone of the destination the user sorts the photo into. A correction made
before them would be a guess written into an original; prep leaves time and place whole for geotag.
RAT-prep_has_no_evidence.section_name: 2. What prep does, and what it leaves alone
sections: 2. What prep does, and what it leaves alone
RAT-prep_has_no_evidence.title: Prep has no evidence for a time or a place

RAT-prep_needs_no_answers.content:
Prep's work — sorting by type and date, setting duplicates aside, recording what is where — follows from the files and
the configuration with nothing left to judge. The questions only the user can answer are about time and place, which are
geotag's; a prep that asked would hold up the inbox on questions it does not need answered.
RAT-prep_needs_no_answers.section_name: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
sections: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
RAT-prep_needs_no_answers.title: Prep has nothing to ask

RAT-prune_harms_nothing.content:
The quarantine holds only spare copies of duplicates, which a sealed workspace still keeps. Deleting them, with the
manifests that list them, touches no photo, library file, control record or row of the database; what each manifest
said is kept in the transformation log and the package. It neither reprocesses the workspace nor adds a batch to it,
so the seal's reasons do not reach it, and the space can be reclaimed.
RAT-prune_harms_nothing.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
RAT-prune_harms_nothing.title: Pruning the quarantine changes nothing controlled

RAT-quarantine_manifest_beside_duplicate.content:
A quarantine manifest says why each file beside it was set aside. Kept in the quarantine folder it describes, it cannot
be parted from those files: whoever looks at a duplicate finds its reason next to it, and pruning a folder removes the
files and their manifest together, leaving no record of files that are gone. What each manifest said is kept in the
transformation log, so pruning loses nothing of the record.
RAT-quarantine_manifest_beside_duplicate.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-quarantine_manifest_beside_duplicate.title: A duplicate and its explanation are not separated

RAT-quarantine_outside_record.content:
A quarantined file is a copy set aside, not part of the workspace the later phases work on; its manifest records why it
was set aside. Kept in the database, it would be listed in the handoff among the photos, and reclaiming quarantine space
— which touches nothing of the record — would change the handoff at the next run and make geotag's work stale.
RAT-quarantine_outside_record.section_name: 10. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
sections: 10. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
RAT-quarantine_outside_record.title: Quarantine is outside the record

RAT-raw_is_master.content:
A camera shooting RAW and JPEG together writes one name with two extensions in one folder. The RAW holds everything the
JPEG does and more, so the JPEG is redundant — kept, not deleted, but set apart from what the user sorts. Only that
evidence is trusted: a name shared within a folder, as the camera wrote it. Another image under the same name is not
the camera's JPEG, and a JPEG and a RAW in different folders, or matched only by time, may be two shots.
RAT-raw_is_master.title: The RAW is the master

RAT-reading_change_detectable.content:
Metadata kept is reused for every unchanged file, so what it depends on must be recorded with it: the file as it was,
and the way it was read. A new extractor, another field set or other options make each record detectably stale, without
being taken for a change in the file — and the record is read again whole ({need}`RAT-reread_on_purpose`).
RAT-reading_change_detectable.section_name: 12. The metadata prep keeps for geotag
sections: 12. The metadata prep keeps for geotag
RAT-reading_change_detectable.title: A change in reading is told apart from a change in the file

RAT-reason_first.content:
The quarantine is never scanned, so a file moved there with no record of why would be invisible to every later run, its
reason lost. Written first, the record survives a crash before the move; the file is still at its source, and the next
run sets it aside again under a new record — the old one at worst a record of a move that did not happen.
RAT-reason_first.title: The reason is written down first

RAT-rebuild_masks_loss.content:
Since prep creates the structure once and never removes a folder, a missing one is evidence the structure was deleted
or moved out-of-band — not a state any phase produces. Silently rebuilding it could mask a real loss: a deleted folder
may have taken organized media with it. Recovering lost media — from an optional pre-mutation snapshot, say — is the
operator's task.
RAT-rebuild_masks_loss.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-rebuild_masks_loss.title: A rebuilt structure could mask a loss

RAT-record_means_stage_reached.content:
The decision records are what the user, the editor and the next stage read. Written at every stage reached — even
when it holds nothing to decide — a record's presence says the stage ran and its status says what is left; its absence
can only mean the stage was not reached. Were an all-automatic stage to write nothing, an absent record would mean either
"nothing to decide" or "never got here", and a record written by a run that stopped at a gate would look like a
decision to act on when there was none.
RAT-record_means_stage_reached.title: A missing record should mean one thing

RAT-record_of_a_finished_run.content:
The handoff tells geotag what prep left, and the log what prep did; written by a run that failed partway, either would
describe a workspace that does not exist. Written only at the end of a run that succeeded, and whole each time, they are
true of the workspace they stand beside, or absent.
RAT-record_of_a_finished_run.title: A record speaks for a finished run

RAT-record_outlives_workspace.content:
The decisions drive a run, but their lasting value is as the record of what was done to the archive and why — and the
workspace is transient: it is merged and set aside, or set aside at any phase boundary without ever advancing. Decisions
are kept for the future only if preserved beyond it, in one known place, rather than scattered in per-file sidecars or,
as with tools that change files and forget, not recorded at all. Since a workspace may stop at any phase, the record
must be whole at each.
RAT-record_outlives_workspace.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-record_outlives_workspace.title: The workspace is transient; the record must not be

RAT-records_attributable.content:
With each phase writing only its own records and carrying earlier ones forward by copy, every phase's output stays a
stable record attributable to it, which no later phase can silently change: complete at its boundary, and evident if
tampered with by what came after. That is why the log is three files, one per phase, not one changed in place. And a
phase that copies its predecessor's record, rather than deriving that history again from other sources, keeps one
account of each phase: a second, rebuilt account could disagree with the first.
RAT-records_attributable.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-records_attributable.title: A record no later phase can silently alter

RAT-recoverable_core.content:
Crash-recovery follows from P1 (an interrupted run must never strand an original half-changed); the diff-based
idempotency also answers F3 — because coverage is partial, one adds more tracks or photos later and re-runs, so a run
must act only on what actually changed.
RAT-recoverable_core.section_name: From P1 + F3 — recoverable, and resumable on incremental input
sections: From P1 + F3 — recoverable, and resumable on incremental input
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-recoverable_core.title: Recoverable core

RAT-redundant_named_like_its_raw.content:
A redundant JPG is the same shot as the RAW kept in the dated folders: named from the same time, the two names show it,
and the JPG's name is checked like any other outside the inbox. With no time to name it from, it is named as any untimed
file is.
RAT-redundant_named_like_its_raw.title: The JPG named like its RAW

RAT-refused_merge_clean.content:
The library is the one place the pipeline cannot simply re-plan from: a photo half placed there, or a summary
claiming a merge that did not happen, would have to be found and undone by hand. Checking every precondition before
the first change makes a refusal free — fix the cause, run merge again — and keeps merge's records describing only
merges that ran.
RAT-refused_merge_clean.title: A refused merge leaves nothing to clean up

RAT-remainder_worklist.content:
An explicit, short **remainder worklist** — what no evidence can locate is collected for a manual pin, not left off the
map.
RAT-remainder_worklist.section_name: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
sections: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-remainder_worklist.title: The true unplaceable set must be surfaced, never silently dropped

RAT-required_means_condition.content:
An operator who requires snapshots has made a rollback point a condition of any change. Going on without one would break
that condition silently, so the run stops before its first change, when stopping costs nothing.
RAT-required_means_condition.title: Required means a condition of changing anything

RAT-reread_on_purpose.content:
The way metadata is read changes only on purpose: more of it is wanted, or what is read must change. Either way every
file is to be read again, and reading it whole — its fingerprint with its metadata — leaves nothing the database says
of it from before the change.
RAT-reread_on_purpose.title: A change in how metadata is read is made on purpose

RAT-rerun_is_safe.content:
Geotag can be re-run freely because a re-run redoes nothing settled: the user's decisions live in geotag's records and
survive their regeneration, what geotag wrote into a file is recognised there, so a corrected time is never corrected
twice and photos added later are corrected beside it, and a name computed from the destination's local time comes out
the same.
RAT-rerun_is_safe.title: Re-running is safe because nothing settled is redone

RAT-rerun_not_frictionless.content:
"Freely re-runnable" does not mean "always a no-op". Any change upstream — not only new media — restales exactly what
depends on it, and may raise new questions about the items it touches; a re-run does that work and no more.
RAT-rerun_not_frictionless.title: Safe is not frictionless

RAT-reseal_automatic.content:
Merge adds to the record finalize packaged, so the existing package no longer describes the whole journey. Since merge
is the workspace's last act, remaking the package once at its end is what the user always wants. Finalize stays its own
command because geotag is freely re-run, and re-packaging after every pass would be wasted.
RAT-reseal_automatic.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
RAT-reseal_automatic.title: Merge is the end, so the package is remade at once

RAT-restore_like_any_file.content:
Moving a file back is the user's way of saying it should not have been set aside. Handled as a new file it is checked
afresh — set aside again if it is still a copy, filed if its twin is gone — and no second path into the pipeline needs
keeping in step with the first ({need}`RAT-fix_through_inbox`). The old record stays: it is history of what that run did.
RAT-restore_like_any_file.title: A restored file goes the way of any file

RAT-retention_serves_the_log.content:
A journey spans many runs — prep, re-prep after moves, repeated geotag passes, merge — so a log rebuilt from the last
run alone would silently lose the rest. What is kept exists to serve the log, and resuming and auditing; it is not an
open-ended store of events.
RAT-retention_serves_the_log.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-retention_serves_the_log.title: Retention serves the log, nothing more

RAT-reverts_are_steps_too.content:
Withdrawing a manual position changes the photo as much as applying one: its position goes back to what it held, or to
none. Logged with what it replaced or restored, every position the photo ever carried can be traced; left out, the log
would show a position the photo no longer has.
RAT-reverts_are_steps_too.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-reverts_are_steps_too.title: Undoing a position is a step too

RAT-reviewer_sees_what_was_touched.content:
A run changes irreplaceable originals. Counted apart, what prep changed and what it only read let the user confirm the
run did what they meant and left alone what it must — at a glance, without reading the journal. A figure the code
fixes in advance is no such confirmation, so the summary reports only what the run counted.
RAT-reviewer_sees_what_was_touched.title: The reviewer sees what was touched

RAT-rollback_chosen_by_hand.content:
A rollback is done by hand, often long after the run. The snapshot must say which plan's changes it precedes, so the
operator can find the right one and tell the phases' snapshots apart.
RAT-rollback_chosen_by_hand.title: A rollback is chosen by hand, later

RAT-safe_at_each_change.content:
That nothing is overwritten, and that an interrupted run is finished by running it again, hold only if each change is
safe when it happens. A half-done move, a half-written file, or a failure recorded as done would break both where no
plan can see it.
RAT-safe_at_each_change.title: Safety and resuming rest on the moment of each change

RAT-safety_net_stays.content:
De-duplication decides by fingerprint; the quarantine is what makes a wrong decision recoverable. Deleting on its own —
after some runs, or some age — would turn a recoverable decision into a loss nobody chose. So the quarantine grows,
visibly, until the user prunes it: by a command of its own, which shows what it would delete before it does.
RAT-safety_net_stays.title: The safety net stays until the user lifts it

RAT-safety_not_on_the_plan.content: No-clobber **re-verified atomically at the moment of each write**, not just at plan time.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-safety_not_on_the_plan.title: Safety cannot rest on the plan being correct

RAT-same_photo_new_fingerprint.content:
A new ImageMagick may decode a photo to a new fingerprint; the photo is the same, and so are its own time and
position. Lost with the old value, they would leave geotag taking the photo's corrected time for its own: a changed
offset would never reach it, a withdrawn one never undo. Prep's log says which old value became which new one; where
it does not say so one for one, no photo's values can be told apart, and geotag stops rather than guess.
RAT-same_photo_new_fingerprint.title: A new decoder does not make a new photo

RAT-same_shape_different_value.content:
Both phases use the same format, but the **value** differs by phase and that difference is intentional. Because the
shape is identical, a file's name changes between phases only when its timestamp is genuinely corrected; an uncorrected
file's provisional and final names coincide, so geotag plans no needless rename for it.
RAT-same_shape_different_value.title: The same shape, a different value, on purpose

RAT-seal_not_folder_state.content:
Photos by destination is empty both in a workspace just sorted and in one merged and finished, so its state cannot say
which a workspace is. A mark written only when merge succeeds whole can — and a merge that left a photo behind writes
none, so it can be finished by running it again.
RAT-seal_not_folder_state.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
RAT-seal_not_folder_state.title: An empty folder means two things; a mark means one

RAT-sealed_is_final.content:
A second batch processed in a merged workspace would interleave with the first's database, logs and package, and its
record would no longer describe one dump. So nothing that could change it runs; the records stay readable; and a dump
dropped there is left untouched and pointed out, for the user to move to a fresh workspace by hand — safer than any
automated move inside a finished workspace.
RAT-sealed_is_final.section_name: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
sections: 13. Merge: the library kept, the workspace sealed
RAT-sealed_is_final.title: A finished workspace is read, not reprocessed

RAT-shutter_time_first.content:
`DateTimeOriginal` is the moment the shutter fired. `CreateDate` is when the file was written, the same moment for a
camera's own file but not for a scan or an export; `ModifyDate` is the last edit, a guess at the making when nothing
else is there. Taking them in that order dates a file as near its making as its metadata allows, and every phase reads
the same one. Some cameras fill a field they cannot set with a placeholder such as `0000:00:00 00:00:00`; that is no
time, and stopping at it would leave a file undated whose next field holds its time.
RAT-shutter_time_first.title: The shutter's time first

RAT-sidecar_orphaned.content:
A sidecar is tied to its photo by name. Prep renames and moves photos, so the sidecar would be left behind under the old
name, its development lost without a word. Development belongs in the library, after merge
({need}`RUL-development_after_merge`); a sidecar arriving with the dump is the user's to keep or discard before prep
goes on.
RAT-sidecar_orphaned.section_name: 6. What prep refuses to work on
sections: 6. What prep refuses to work on
RAT-sidecar_orphaned.title: A sidecar would be orphaned

RAT-size_time_sign_change.content:
Decoding a photo to fingerprint it is the costliest step prep takes, so it is done once per file and kept. Any write to
a file changes its size or its modification time, and both are read without opening it: an unchanged pair says the
fingerprint kept still describes the file, a changed one that it may not.
RAT-size_time_sign_change.title: Size and time are the cheap sign of change

RAT-snapshot_is_extra.content:
**Snapshots are an optional extra safety layer, not a requirement.** The pipeline operates fully and safely without
them: correctness and recoverability rest on the journal, recoverable quarantine, no-clobber operations, and
filesystem-as-truth reconciliation. Snapshots add a clean-slate rollback path on top of those for operators whose
filesystem supports it; they are not the basis of the safety model.
RAT-snapshot_is_extra.title: A snapshot is an extra layer, not the safety model

RAT-snapshot_just_before.title: A rollback point is the state just before the change

RAT-snapshot_name_early.content:
A snapshot's name the snapshot tool would refuse is found when the configuration is read, not when the snapshot is
taken, so a bad name never surprises an execution midway.
RAT-snapshot_name_early.section_name: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
sections: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
RAT-snapshot_name_early.title: A snapshot fails before anything changes, not midway

RAT-sort_costs_no_reading.content:
Sorting photos into destinations is the user's own work, done between runs, and prep must plan again after it. Were each
moved photo read again, every sort would cost a decode of everything sorted. A move made by hand keeps a file's size,
time and name, so that triple, read without opening the file, says which file it was; where it fits more than one, prep
does not guess, and reads the file as new.
RAT-sort_costs_no_reading.section_name: 10. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
sections: 10. Files the user moves, and the plan memo
RAT-sort_costs_no_reading.title: Sorting costs no reading

RAT-speed_is_the_machines.content:
Running fingerprints and metadata reads in parallel only saves time; how many at once depends on the machine, which may
change between runs of one workspace. A plan that differed with it would depend on where it was made; recorded, the
count would make two equal plans differ. So the work is listed and gathered in a fixed order, and the count is kept
nowhere.
RAT-speed_is_the_machines.section_name: 17. Concurrency, determinism, and what a run shows
sections: 17. Concurrency, determinism, and what a run shows
RAT-speed_is_the_machines.title: Speed is the machine's, the plan is the workspace's

RAT-stage_cut_points.content:
**The exact decomposition into seven stages** rather than six or eight. The *principle* of discrete inspectable
checkpoints is forced (P1+F3); the specific cut points are judgment.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-stage_cut_points.title: The exact decomposition into stages

RAT-stray_as_it_came.content:
A file of no media class is not the pipeline's to process ({need}`RAT-strays_not_the_pipelines`); it leaves the inbox
so that the inbox ends empty, and goes where the user can find it as it was — at the place it had in the dump, under the
name it came with, in the run's own folder so no two runs' strays meet.
RAT-stray_as_it_came.title: A stray is the user's, untouched

RAT-strays_not_the_pipelines.content:
A stray is a file cartographer does not understand — a document, a sidecar it has no use for. Recorded beside the media,
it would make cartographer answer for what it cannot reason about; parked whole, it waits for the user to keep or clear
it, and clearing it costs the record nothing.
RAT-strays_not_the_pipelines.section_name: 3. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
sections: 3. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
RAT-strays_not_the_pipelines.title: A stray is not the pipeline's to answer for

RAT-structure_from_the_tool.content:
The user edits these records a few times a year, by hand or in the editor. A field they had to add would need its exact
name and place remembered, and one mistyped would be a decision lost or misread; laid out by the tool, every decision is
one value to fill in, its place already right.
RAT-structure_from_the_tool.section_name: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
sections: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
RAT-structure_from_the_tool.title: The tool lays out, the user fills in

RAT-structure_names_reserved.content:
A managed folder's name is reserved for the structure. Moving a folder of that name into the inbox would nest a managed
folder inside another, where nothing would look for it, and leave its place to be made again empty beside it.
RAT-structure_names_reserved.section_name: 3. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
sections: 3. The workspace’s first run, and the strays
RAT-structure_names_reserved.title: The structure's names are reserved

RAT-superseded_plans_recoverable.content:
Setting the prior artifact aside keeps a superseded plan and any authored decisions recoverable; writing nothing on an
unchanged re-run means the iterative decision-editing loop does not accumulate redundant backups.
RAT-superseded_plans_recoverable.section_name: 4. The control records, apart from the media
sections: 4. The control records, apart from the media
RAT-superseded_plans_recoverable.title: A superseded plan stays recoverable; an unchanged one adds nothing

RAT-surgical_staleness.content:
Collapsing all staleness to a single whole-file hash would needlessly restale unrelated artifacts on any edit, and is
explicitly not done.
RAT-surgical_staleness.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
RAT-surgical_staleness.title: Surgical staleness: one hash for everything would restale everything

RAT-temps_are_debris.content:
Merge holds the library's lock, so a temporary copy found in a folder it places into was left by an interrupted earlier
merge, never one being written now. It bears no photo's name, so it does no harm either way: clearing it keeps the
library free of litter — hygiene, not safety.
RAT-temps_are_debris.title: A temporary copy left behind is debris

RAT-time_name_recomputed.content:
A file's time and name are not rolled back when a decision is withdrawn but recomputed in place: reverting them would
un-position a file the user has already organized.
RAT-time_name_recomputed.section_name: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
sections: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
RAT-time_name_recomputed.title: A time and a name are recomputed, not reverted

RAT-total_coverage_cascade.content:
This choice fights F3: tracks cover only *part* of the library, but the output must be *whole*. That gap is what forces
the fallback machinery to exist: without P4, tracks alone would be the entire story and everything below would be
unnecessary.
RAT-total_coverage_cascade.section_name: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
sections: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-total_coverage_cascade.title: Total-coverage cascade

RAT-touched_since_geotag.content:
Geotag's gates held when geotag ran; merge runs later, often much later, and the user may have dropped a new dump into
the inbox, moved a photo back to photos by date, or put a video or a development folder among the photos by
destination in between. Merge is the step after which none of that can be undone cheaply: what it places is in the
library, beside photos it must never disturb. So it asks the workspace again, not geotag's record of it. The folders
the gates leave out are the residue the library never receives; they stay in the workspace, as they would for geotag.
RAT-touched_since_geotag.title: The workspace may have been touched since geotag

RAT-track_points_read_exactly.content:
A track's points become positions and clock offsets; a time read an hour wrong, or in a zone guessed, would place
photos and correct cameras by that hour, and look like evidence. Recorders write the same instant in several valid
forms, so each is read as the instant it is; one stating no zone could be any of them and is not used. Skipping a
point silently would let a track whose every point was rejected pass for an empty one, and the user would never learn
why the photos it should have placed were not.
RAT-track_points_read_exactly.title: A track is evidence only where it can be read

RAT-track_squeezed.content:
**Direct match → interpolation between points → bounded extrapolation off the ends**, each used before falling back to
manual.
RAT-track_squeezed.section_name: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
sections: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-track_squeezed.title: Every placeable point of the track must be squeezed out

RAT-tracks_are_geotags_evidence.content:
The tracks are evidence for a photo's time and place, and only geotag decides those: prep never plans a time or a
position, so it has no use for them. A phase that read them would also have to treat every change to them as a change
to its own records.
RAT-tracks_are_geotags_evidence.section_name: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
sections: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
RAT-tracks_are_geotags_evidence.title: The tracks are geotag's evidence

RAT-tracks_change_the_answers.content:
The tracks are evidence for the clock offsets and positions geotag proposes, and a track added, corrected or removed can
change them. A decision made against the old tracks, or a plan built from them, could then be wrong while still looking
settled; the tracks' fingerprint in each record turns the change into staleness instead of letting it pass unseen.
RAT-tracks_change_the_answers.section_name: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
sections: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
RAT-tracks_change_the_answers.title: Changed tracks can change the answers

RAT-tracks_kept_outside.content:
The shared rule that makes it safe for geotag alone to own the tracks is where they live. Kept outside the managed
folders, prep's normal scan never encounters them, so they can never be taken for files of no media class, or swept
into the inbox and organized.
RAT-tracks_kept_outside.section_name: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
sections: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
RAT-tracks_kept_outside.title: Where the tracks live is what keeps them geotag's

RAT-tracks_never_strays.content:
Parked among the strays, a track could be deleted when the strays are cleared in bulk, and a lost track is evidence no
re-run can recover. Refusing to run leaves it where the user put it until they move it to the tracks' location.
RAT-tracks_never_strays.section_name: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
sections: 7. The tracks, kept outside the managed folders
RAT-tracks_never_strays.title: A track among the strays could be deleted with them

RAT-trips_revisit.content:
A trip often comes back to its places: a town visited from the same hotel day after day, a square crossed morning and
evening, with a track for every one. Any of those visits passes where a photo was taken, and which passed closest is
chance. Matched to the wrong visit, a whole day's photos are corrected by a day, or by hours — written into the
originals, named by the wrong time, placed on the wrong walk — with no sign anything is off. When the photos cannot
say which visit is theirs, only the user, who remembers the day, can.
RAT-trips_revisit.section_name: 19. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
sections: 19. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
RAT-trips_revisit.title: A trip comes back to its places

RAT-unknown_is_not_unchanged.content:
A dependency that cannot be checked gives no assurance either way. Counting it unchanged would let a failure to look
stand for proof that nothing moved: a file deleted since the plan, a record a crash left behind, a plan recording
nothing would all pass. Refusing costs a re-plan; trusting could cost a photo its place or its record.
RAT-unknown_is_not_unchanged.section_name: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
sections: 8. Nothing used once what it came from has changed
RAT-unknown_is_not_unchanged.title: Failing to look is no proof that nothing changed

RAT-unlisted_media_noticed.content:
The media lists are the user's configuration, and a camera may write a format they never listed. Its photos would be set
aside as strays, recoverably but without a word. Asking the files' content what they are catches that, and leaves the
choice — to list the extension and plan again — with the user; the warning blocks nothing and changes no list.
RAT-unlisted_media_noticed.section_name: 6. What prep refuses to work on
sections: 6. What prep refuses to work on
RAT-unlisted_media_noticed.title: A format the lists missed is noticed

RAT-untimed_set_apart.content:
Prep cannot invent a time, and a file with none has no day to be filed under: it waits apart, flat, until the user
gives it one. Its untimed name keeps the name it came with, the user's only way to tell which file it was.
RAT-untimed_set_apart.title: A file with no time cannot be dated

RAT-valid_is_not_unchanged.content:
A fingerprint tells whether a value changed, not whether it makes sense. A value can match its fingerprint and still be
meaningless or dangerous, or be freshly typed and wrong; and a value valid in one run can be edited before the next. So
both checks are needed, every time.
RAT-valid_is_not_unchanged.section_name: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
sections: 14. Every value the user writes is checked
RAT-valid_is_not_unchanged.title: A current value can still be wrong

RAT-videos_kept_not_corrected.content:
The pipeline's aim is photos placed in time and on the map. Videos arrive in the same dumps; prep organizes them by date
so they are neither lost nor scattered, not because the pipeline means to correct them — so they keep a folder of their
own, out of the sort.
RAT-videos_kept_not_corrected.section_name: 2. What prep does, and what it leaves alone
sections: 2. What prep does, and what it leaves alone
RAT-videos_kept_not_corrected.title: Videos are kept, not corrected

RAT-what_was_reviewed_happens.content:
What the user reviewed — the plan, its dry run — is what must happen. An execution that decided afresh would act on a
judgement nobody saw, and a difference between the plan and what was done could not be explained from the record.
Deciding again is planning's work: when the workspace has moved on, the plan is stale and refused, and the user plans
again.
RAT-what_was_reviewed_happens.section_name: 16. Nothing changed outside a validated plan
sections: 16. Nothing changed outside a validated plan
RAT-what_was_reviewed_happens.title: What was reviewed is what happens

RAT-which_folder_library.content:
**The downstream library, not the tree.** A *hierarchical* destination tree is **forced**, not chosen: the timezone /
offset / GPS-fallback cascade rides on the folder nesting, so a flat or tag-based layout would make inheritance
impossible and drive the per-photo workload straight back up. What is actually free is only *which* folder-based
library consumes the result — digiKam, or any other — and the cosmetic naming of the levels.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-which_folder_library.title: The downstream library, not the tree

RAT-why_beside_what.content:
A step alone says what happened to a photo — its time moved by three hours — not why. Years later, the decision behind
it is what tells a right correction from a mistake; named beside the step, it is found without searching records that
may be long gone with the workspace.
RAT-why_beside_what.section_name: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
sections: 12. The record of what was done, kept beyond the workspace
RAT-why_beside_what.title: The why beside the what

RAT-why_did_this_change.content:
For irreplaceable photos, a user who distrusts opaque, automatic change must always be able to answer *why did this
change happen?* — and to change the answer. So the tool proposes and the user decides, the decision stays in a durable
record that the change can be traced back to, and revising the record revises the result.
RAT-why_did_this_change.section_name: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
sections: 11. Nothing changes that the user did not write down
RAT-why_did_this_change.title: A user who distrusts opaque mutation can always ask why

RAT-workspace_keeps_its_settings.content:
A workspace's runs, spread over days or weeks, must all read the settings it was set up with, or a later run could
process the same files differently from an earlier one. The seed defaults belong to the installed program, which may be
upgraded or redeployed meanwhile; so they are copied once into the workspace, where they can be read, edited and
archived, and from then on the copy governs, not the program.
RAT-workspace_keeps_its_settings.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
RAT-workspace_keeps_its_settings.title: A workspace keeps the settings it started with

RAT-workspace_not_recycled.content:
Even with photos by destination empty, a merged workspace keeps its database, ledgers, caches, snapshots and sealed
record. Starting afresh keeps each workspace's record about one batch.
RAT-workspace_not_recycled.title: A merged workspace is not a clean slate

RAT-workspace_one_filesystem.content:
On one filesystem every move a workspace sees is a single rename: nothing to copy, nothing to verify, no temporary copy
to leave behind. A workspace is one place made for one ingest, so nothing needs it spread over volumes; one that is
would turn prep's ordinary moves into copies, slower and less safe. Only the library is a place apart, and only merge
crosses into it. Checking every run, not once, catches a volume mounted into the workspace since the last.
RAT-workspace_one_filesystem.title: Within a workspace, every move is one rename

RUL-anchor_consensus.content:
The offset proposed from a camera's GPS SHALL be the one the most of its photos agree on — each photo counting every
time the tracks passed where it was taken — never an average, and never one photo's closest match outvoting the rest.
RUL-anchor_consensus.section_name: 19. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
sections: 19. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
RUL-anchor_consensus.title: The offset is the one most photos agree on

RUL-anchor_offset_auto_as_configured.content:
A clock offset proposed from a camera's own GPS positions SHALL take effect without the user's answer only as the
configuration's settings for one anchor and for several allow, and never while its anchors disagree.
RUL-anchor_offset_auto_as_configured.title: A camera's offset from its own GPS applies itself only as configured

RUL-anchor_within_clock_error.content:
A track SHALL anchor a camera's clock only at times within the largest clock error the configuration allows of the
camera's own time, whatever timezone the camera was set to.
RUL-anchor_within_clock_error.section_name: 19. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
sections: 19. Clock offsets from the camera’s own GPS
RUL-anchor_within_clock_error.title: A track anchors a clock only within the plausible error

RUL-any_config_change_replans.content:
Any change to the configuration, in whatever area, SHALL make stale every plan made before it — prep's plan, geotag's
executable plan and merge's plan — so that none of them is executed.
RUL-any_config_change_replans.section_name: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
sections: 3. One configuration, kept in the workspace
RUL-any_config_change_replans.title: Any configuration change restales the plan

RUL-band_misplacement_blocks.content: A video in photos by date or photos by destination, or a photo in videos by date, SHALL block prep's plan.
RUL-band_misplacement_blocks.section_name: 6. What prep refuses to work on
sections: 6. What prep refuses to work on
RUL-band_misplacement_blocks.title: A file in the other kind's folder blocks prep

RUL-blockers_all_reported.content: Prep SHALL report every blocker it finds, each naming what blocks, never skipping one silently.
RUL-blockers_all_reported.section_name: 6. What prep refuses to work on
sections: 6. What prep refuses to work on
RUL-blockers_all_reported.title: Every blocker is reported

RUL-by_date_in_day_folder.content:
