TST-move_aware-rehash_summary_flags_mtim.title: A previously-cached file whose mtime changed is re-fingerprinted and reported as an UNEXPECTED re-hash, reason `mtime-changed`, with the file in the first-N sample and the counts in the run report.

TST-no_clobber-execute_time_no_clobber_p.title: test execute time no clobber preserves existing

TST-plan_freshness-json_artifact_dep_fre.title: test json artifact dep fresh changed missing

TST-plan_memo-a_broken_memo_degrades_ins.title: The memo is an accelerator, never a dependency: a corrupt memo database costs the decode it was saving and nothing else — the plan still completes.

TST-plan_memo-changed_file_is_not_reused.title: A memo row faces the same freshness gate as a cache row: bump the mtime and it is rejected, the file is re-decoded, and the re-hash diagnostic names a reason rather than staying silent.

TST-plan_memo-engine_change_invalidates_.title: The memo stores the engine version bound to each pixel signature, so an ImageMagick bump restales memo rows exactly as it restales cache rows.

TST-plan_memo-executed_cache_wins_over_t.title: A cache row is the executed state and always outranks a memo row for the same path: after execute, reuse is attributed to the cache (memo_reused 0), not to the memo.

TST-plan_memo-memo_drops_paths_it_no_lon.title: The memo tracks the workspace instead of growing forever: a file that disappears loses its row.

TST-plan_memo-memo_skips_records_it_coul.title: Only complete observations are stored. A record without a metadata row could not satisfy the all-or-nothing freshness gate, so storing it would buy nothing and relabel its re-hash reason.

TST-plan_memo-plan_does_not_write_the_wo.title: The memo must not become a back door into the cache: planning still leaves file_cache empty, and the memo lives in its own database file.

TST-plan_memo-replan_without_execute_reu.title: The point of the memo: plan, do NOT execute, plan again — the second plan decodes nothing. Before the memo this re-hashed the whole workspace, because cache rows are written by execute.

TST-plan_memo-the_memo_never_changes_the.title: The same workspace plans to the same operations with the memo empty, reused, or gone.

TST-plan_memo-the_memo_proves_no_move.title: A file read by a plan never executed and then moved into photos by destination is not recognized as moved: the memo's entry for its old path is no record of it, and it is read as new.

TST-plan_place-no_plan_location_option.title: test no command takes a plan location

TST-plan_place-unchanged_replan_writes_n.title: test identical rewrite writes nothing and backs up nothing

TST-prep_log-a_photo_moved_under_a_new_i.title: A photo the user sorts into photos by destination while ImageMagick changes, its fingerprint's value changing with it, keeps its whole history: the entry moves to the new value and records the user's move — none left behind claiming the photo is still where prep put it.

TST-prep_log-a_retaken_fingerprint_keeps.title: A photo fingerprinted again by another method, its value changed, keeps its history: the entry moves to the new value, with a step saying so — no orphan under the old value, nothing partial.

TST-prep_log-every_move_names_where_it_c.title: The journey keeps the chain of names and places: each move and rename records where the photo came from as well as where it went, so the first step holds its original path in the dump.

TST-prep_log-log_is_deterministic_and_in.title: test log is deterministic and in control dir

TST-prep_log-media_journey_keyed_by_fing.title: test media journey keyed by fingerprint

TST-prep_log-missing_history_warns_and_m.title: test missing history warns and marks partial

TST-prep_log-prep_log_entries_are_derive.title: §16.1 item 4: the prep log is DERIVED from the validated plan + journals and introduces no new authority — its facts trace back to plan operations. Assert the logged final destination equals a destination the plan actually planned, and the extension-normalization step's 'from' name matches the plan's rename source — the log records nothing the plan/journal did not establish.

TST-prep_log-recognized_move_appends_mov.title: test recognized move appends moved to by dest

TST-prep_log-strays_and_other_not_logged.title: test strays and other not logged

TST-prep_pipeline-a_duplicate_is_set_asi.title: A duplicate goes to quarantine from its dump path under its dump name — no rename first — and its record names that path.

TST-prep_pipeline-a_file_back_from_missi.title: A file sent back to the inbox with still no time returns to missing metadata under the name it had there: the untimed mark is not taken twice.

TST-prep_pipeline-a_file_sent_back_is_re.title: A filed file the user moves back into the inbox is filed again under the name it had; the row of that path is the move's, not a ghost to prune.

TST-prep_pipeline-a_quarantined_file_lea.title: A duplicate set aside has no row in the database and no entry in the handoff; reclaiming the quarantine leaves the next plan nothing to do.

TST-prep_pipeline-a_redumped_pair_settle.title: A RAW+JPEG pair dumped again is set aside as duplicates in the run that finds it — the JPEG too — keeping the copies already filed; the next run has nothing to do.

TST-prep_pipeline-a_stray_keeps_its_plac.title: test a stray keeps its place and name

TST-prep_pipeline-an_inbox_file_takes_it.title: An inbox file is filed in one move that lowercases its extension: no rename inside the inbox.

TST-prep_pipeline-an_untimed_redundant_j.title: A JPEG set aside beside its RAW with no recorded time takes its untimed name, flat — the mark once, however it came.

TST-prep_pipeline-copies_in_one_folder_k.title: test copies in one folder keep the first by path

TST-prep_pipeline-only_the_jpeg_beside_a.title: A RAW sets aside the JPEG of its name in its folder — `.jpg` or `.jpeg` — and no other image.

TST-prep_split-execute_rejects_any_opera.title: test execute rejects any operation in by dest[0-sources/a.jpg-6-photos-by-dest/Trip/a.jpg]

TST-prep_split-execute_rejects_forbidden.title: test execute rejects forbidden operation types

TST-report-duplicate_split_against_by_de.title: test duplicate split against by dest

TST-report-recognized_move_counted_in_re.title: test recognized move counted in report

TST-serve-save_refuses_while_a_run_holds.title: A save changes the workspace, so it takes the workspace's lock: while a run holds it, the save refuses and writes nothing — it cannot land between a geotag plan's read and its rewrite. Once the run ends, the same save goes through, and leaves the lock free.

TST-serve-serve_points_out_a_dump_in_a_s.title: test serve points out a dump in a sealed workspace

TST-serve-serve_refuses_a_sealed_workspa.title: test serve refuses a sealed workspace

TST-snapshot-failed_run_leaves_prior_sna.title: test failed run leaves prior snapshot intact

TST-snapshot-snapshot_leaves_no_temp_and.title: test snapshot leaves no temp and refreshes on rerun

TST-stale_plan-a_failed_journal_save_lea.title: The journal is replaced whole: a save that fails partway leaves the journal as the previous save wrote it.

TST-stale_plan-a_plan_made_by_other_code.title: A saved plan records the code that made it; execute refuses it once the code differs — or when it records none — before any change.

TST-stale_plan-config_change_rejects_pla.title: test config change rejects plan at execute

TST-stale_plan-new_file_since_planning_r.title: Prep §14.3 item 2: a file that appears anywhere prep scans between plan and execute is unplanned, so the plan is stale — refused before any mutation, the planned file and the newcomer left in place.

TST-stale_plan-replan_incorporates_new_f.title: After the refusal a new plan takes the newcomer in, fingerprinting only it: the refused plan's fingerprints are reused from the memo (prep §10.3). Metadata is read a folder at a time, so a file is re-read only when it shares a folder with one that needs reading; here they are apart.

TST-stale_plan-the_build_and_its_checkou.title: The code's fingerprint is the same whether the package runs from its checkout or from the zipapp built from it, and changes with any file the zipapp ships.

TST-stale_plan-track_file_since_planning.title: A track dropped in after planning is refused like at planning: the rescan blocks on it.

TST-strays-a_file_of_no_media_class_outs.title: Prep moves a file of no media class to the strays folder only from the inbox. Anywhere else — an extension taken off the lists, a file put there by hand — it stops the plan, naming the file, and the file stays where it is.

TST-strays-every_track_format_blocks_pre.title: Shared contract §8: a track in any format, not only the GPX geotag reads, is never media — it blocks the plan and stays in the dump, never parked in 1-strays.

TST-strays-prep_never_reads_the_tracks.title: Prep resolves gpx_root to check where it lies, and does nothing more with it: it never lists, walks or opens anything beneath it, and never builds geotag's GPX index.

TST-strays-stray_media_detection_silent_.title: test stray media detection silent when exiftool absent

TST-strays-stray_media_detection_warns_o.title: test stray media detection warns only for media mime

TST-strays-stray_not_fingerprinted_and_n.title: test stray not fingerprinted and not cached

TST-strays-track_file_blocks_prep_and_st.title: Shared contract §8: a track is never media. A `.gpx` anywhere prep inventories — the 0-sources dump or a managed folder — blocks the plan and is left where it is: no operation moves it (above all not into 1-strays, where clearing the strays would delete it), it is never fingerprinted, and the blocked plan cannot be executed.

TST-workspace_prep-a_blocker_is_reported.title: §6.2 final line ('Blockers are reported textually; the workflow does not silently skip them'). With a forbidden sidecar present alongside a perfectly organizable photo, prep must (a) SURFACE the blocker as descriptive text in plan.blockers and (b) refuse the whole run at execute — it never silently drops the blocker and proceeds to organize the valid photo. Asserts the never-skip principle itself, not merely that some blocker string appears.

TST-workspace_prep-already_lowercase_ext.title: §13 item 3: prep does not re-normalize an already-normalized extension. A file already named with a lowercase `.jpg` must produce NO extension-normalization rename op (no two-step temp rename, no rename_no_clobber on it) — distinct from the idempotency rerun, which asserts the whole plan is empty rather than isolating the extension non-renaming.

TST-workspace_prep-directory_symlink_at_.title: A directory symlink at the root of an UNINITIALIZED workspace must be flagged as a forbidden symlink at PLAN time, never followed. os.path.isdir() follows a directory symlink, so the old isdir-first order let os.walk(path) traverse the external target and inventory (and plan a move for) files outside the workspace — the pipeline escape the spec forbids.

TST-workspace_prep-empty_sources_is_stea.title: §6.2 (item 7, final clause): an EMPTY 0-sources is the normal steady end-state (Section 18), NOT a missing-folder condition. On an initialized workspace whose 0-sources is present but empty (every managed folder intact), prep plans cleanly — zero operations, and crucially NO 'non-conforming'/'missing folder' blocker naming 0-sources. (Distinct from test_missing_managed_folder..., which DELETES folders; here 0-sources exists and is just empty.)

TST-workspace_prep-every_executed_operat.title: Execution records every operation it carries out in the run's journal — moves, renames and setting duplicates aside alike — each with its outcome, and no operation the plan does not hold.

TST-workspace_prep-gpx_root_inside_manag.title: Shared contract §8: a gpx_root configured inside the managed tree is an invalid configuration — prep refuses to plan, naming the field, and nothing in the workspace moves.

TST-workspace_prep-init_does_not_move_a_.title: Reserved-name guard (prep §6.2): on an INIT run a base entry whose name collides with a managed folder (e.g. an as-arrived dump dir named `5-photos-by-date`) is treated AS that managed folder — NEVER inventoried as a dump and moved beneath itself into 0-sources/5-photos-by-date (a silent data-shuffling hazard). Assert no init-move op relocates it under 0-sources.

TST-workspace_prep-init_move_excludes_ma.title: §3.1: init's base-dump consolidation moves genuine root dumps into 0-sources but EXCLUDES the managed 0-6 folders and the control/dot directories (.photos-ingest, .git). A real root dump file IS moved (proving the init move ran), while a pre-existing managed folder (with media already in it) and a .git dir are NEVER relocated beneath 0-sources. (The reserved-names test covers a dump dir NAMED like a managed folder; this covers actually-present managed + control dirs.)

TST-workspace_prep-initialized_root_dotf.title: The top level of an INITIALIZED workspace holds the managed folders and hidden entries (shared contract §4): a root dotfile (a file manager's `.directory` or `.DS_Store`) is not a misplaced dump — no block — and, the root being no dump area once initialized, no operation touches it.

TST-workspace_prep-missing_managed_folde.title: An activated workspace (guard present) missing managed 0-6 folder(s) is non-conforming — prep hard-stops with a blocker rather than silently recreating them (which could mask lost media).

TST-workspace_prep-plan_is_non_mutating.title: Planning changes nothing: with work to do, every file of a workspace past its first run — media and records, the workspace database among them — is byte-identical afterwards; the only file it adds is the fingerprint memo it keeps for later runs. (This writes no plan: the command saves it, not the planner.)

TST-workspace_prep-prep_blocks_a_link_un.title: Prep never changes 6-photos-by-dest, yet it is the gatekeeper for links there: a link under it blocks prep's plan, so no handoff is built while one is present.

arch.description: Mapping of uml key to uml content.

constraints.description: List of constraint names, which are defined for this need.

constraints_error.description: An error message set if any constraint failed, and `error_message` field is set in config.

constraints_passed.description: True if all constraints passed, False if any failed, None if not yet checked.

constraints_results.description: Mapping of constraint name, to check name, to result, None if not yet checked.

content.description: The main content of the need.

docname.description: Name of the document where the need is defined (None if external).

doctype.description: The markup type of the content, denoted by the suffix of the source file, e.g. '.rst'.

external_css.description: CSS class name, added to the external reference.

external_url.description: URL of the need, if it is an external need.

has_dead_links.description: True if any links reference need ids that are not found in the need list.

has_forbidden_dead_links.description: True if any links reference need ids that are not found in the need list, and the link type does not allow dead links.

is_external.description: If true, no node is created and need is referencing external url.

is_import.description: If true, the need was derived from an import.

is_modified.description: Whether the need was modified by needextend.

jinja_content.description: Whether the content was pre-processed by jinja.

layout.description: Key of the layout, which is used to render the need.

lineno.description: Line number where the need is defined (None if external).

parts.description: Mapping of parts, a.k.a. sub-needs, IDs to data that overrides the need's data

post_template.description: The template key, if the post_content was created from a jinja template.

pre_template.description: The template key, if the pre_content was created from a jinja template.

signature.description: Derived from a docutils desc_name node.

style.description: Comma-separated list of CSS classes (all appended by `needs_style_`).

template.description: The template key, if the content was created from a jinja template.
